---
name: reference_agent_run_context_and_lobu_urls
description: "What the per-turn run-context block carries, and the two wrong sources for the Lobu link origin (DISPATCHER_URL, request Host) that both look right and both break"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 9b2cbf0b-681a-45b4-93cf-d91a16522d4c
  modified: 2026-07-29T18:17:01.616Z
---

`buildRunContextBlock` (`packages/agent-worker/src/runtime/session-runner.ts`)
prepends a `## This conversation` block to the **user** turn — never the system
prompt, because it varies per turn and would bust the cached prefix. Extending it
is therefore free in cache terms; extending the system prompt is not.

After #2322 it renders: Platform, Channel, Thread, Triggered by, Agent,
Conversation, Lobu, Link. Every field is omitted when absent — never "unknown".

## The link origin: two sources that look right and are wrong

Every Lobu URL is `<webOrigin>/<orgSlug>/…`. The slug is reachable by the agent
via `client.organizations.current()`. The origin must come from the gateway's
configured `publicGatewayUrl`, shipped through `/session-context`:

- **NOT `DISPATCHER_URL`** — the worker reaches the gateway over the INTERNAL
  cluster address (repo fixture: `http://gateway:8080`). Renders a host no user
  can open. Passes every unit test.
- **NOT `getRequestBaseUrl(c)`** — same reason: the worker calls that endpoint,
  so the request Host is a cluster name.

**Strip a trailing `/lobu`, and ONLY `/lobu`.** Prod runs
`PUBLIC_GATEWAY_URL=https://app.lobu.ai/lobu`; the gateway is mounted under that
prefix, the frontend routes these links target are not, so an unstripped base
404s on every link. A different mount path is **preserved**, matching
`buildAgentSettingsUrl` — an agent whose links disagree with the server's is
worse than both being wrong the same way. `toPublicWebOrigin` in
`packages/server/src/utils/url-builder.ts` is the single implementation.

## Traps

- `agentId` must come from the worker, never `platformMetadata.agentId` —
  untrusted metadata could otherwise name the agent to itself. All fields run
  through the control-char/length sanitizer: no field may forge a `## heading`
  or `- list item`.
- `platform === "api"` returns `""` deliberately. pi records whatever string
  goes to `session.prompt()` into the transcript, so an injected block replays in
  the web UI attributed to the user.
- **Behavior/scheduled runs render NO `Triggered by` line** — scheduled dispatch
  sets `platformMetadata.senderId` while the block reads
  `senderDisplayName ?? senderUsername`. So an agent cannot distinguish an
  automated run from a human message except by a missing line. No behavior id
  reaches worker `platformMetadata` anywhere on `origin/main`; a `Behavior:` line
  needs dispatch-site plumbing. UNBUILT.

Canonical URL shapes: conversation `/<slug>/agents/<id>/conversations/<convId>`,
agent settings `…/settings`, behavior `…/behaviors/<id>`, connector
`/<slug>/connectors/<key>`, memory `/<slug>/memory?…`.

Related: [[project_system_prompt_override_is_inert]], [[reference_org_composite_pk_scoping]].

Both answers, with evidence from your actual DM.

## 1. Yes, "View in Lobu ↗" is still there

`packages/server/src/gateway/connections/lobu-answer-link.ts:17` defines the label; `chat-response-bridge.ts:441-452` appends it to `payload.finalText` at completion, but only for post-once strategies (Slack, `deliversAtCompletion = true`). It landed in #2137 and has never been touched since — `git log origin/main -- lobu-answer-link.ts` shows exactly one commit.

The thing you're remembering is a different change that was **additive, not a replacement**. #2322 added `buildRunContextBlock` (`packages/agent-worker/src/runtime/session-runner.ts`), which prepends a `## This conversation` block to the user turn carrying Platform / Channel / Thread / Triggered by / Agent / Conversation / Lobu / Link. That gave the agent the ids and gateway URLs so it can answer "where am I", but nobody deleted the footer afterwards.

## 2. The two messages are a real bug, and the footer isn't the cause

From your DM with Lobu (`D095U1QV667`), 2026-07-30:

```
23:57:27  you    e2e check from Claude Code — are you there?
23:57:37  Lobu   Buradayım, çalışıyorum ✅ — CRM ajanı ayakta, ne lazım?
23:57:43  Lobu   E2e kontrolünü yanıtladım — ayakta olduğumu teyit ettim.
                 [View in Lobu ↗](https://app.lobu.ai/community/agents/crm/conversations/slack%3AD095U1QV667)
```

Identical shape on 07-27 ("Selam! 👋 Ben pi, buradayım…" then "Selamını yanıtladım ✅ …").

The second message is the one carrying the footer, so it's unambiguously the `chat-response-bridge` completion path. The first is the agent replying in-band during the run via the internal `/conversations/send` tool (`packages/server/src/gateway/routes/internal/conversations.ts:129`). Slack's strategy posts nothing before completion — `handleDelta` only buffers — so nothing else in the gateway could have produced it.

So the sequence is: the agent posts its real answer as a tool call, then ends its turn with a past-tense *report* about having answered, and the bridge delivers that report as a second Slack message. You get the answer, then a summary of the answer. The footer just makes the redundant one look official.

Two independent fixes, and they're not the same decision:
- **The duplicate**: suppress bridge delivery when the agent already posted into that same conversation during the run (the send route already knows `target.connectionId` + `threadId`). This is the actual defect.
- **The footer**: now that run-context ships the conversation URL to the agent, dropping it is defensible — but that's a separate call, and removing it won't fix the duplicate.

One other thing the search surfaced: the org slug in those links drifted from `/lobu-crm` (07-27) to `/community` (07-30) for the same agent and same DM. That may be intentional, but if not, the 07-27 links are now dead.

- Footer still ships (95): read the file and the call site on `origin/main`, plus live Slack messages containing it.
- Message 2 = bridge completion path (95): the footer is only appended there.
- Message 1 = agent's own `/conversations/send` (75): structural elimination — no other gateway path posts a plain first-person reply pre-completion — but I did not read the run transcript to see the tool call itself.
- No code changed this session; nothing built or run.

**Next actions**
1. Pull the transcript for run at `2026-07-30 23:57` to confirm the `/conversations/send` tool call, which would take that 75 to certainty.
2. Decide the duplicate fix: suppress `handleCompletion` when the run already posted to the same `conversationId`, vs. instructing the agent not to use `/conversations/send` for the reply it's already returning.
3. Separately decide whether to delete the footer now that `buildRunContextBlock` carries the link.
4. Check whether the `lobu-crm` → `community` slug change was intentional, and whether old links 404.

content.text:
Verified the whole path. Before I write code, let me answer your question directly, because it's the crux.

**"Do we know the summary isn't needed?"** — we can't know that semantically, and we shouldn't try. Classifying "is this text a summary" is exactly the text-matcher-as-boundary trap. But we don't need to, because there's a structural fact that's decidable: **the agent already delivered into the same conversation during the run.** When that's true, `finalText` is a report about a message the user has already read. When it's false — the agent posted to `#general` because you asked it to — `finalText` *is* the answer and must still be delivered.

So the rule is target-scoped, not "did it call `send_message`".

And the resolution is cheap, because the pieces already exist:
- The worker token already carries the run's triggering `conversationId` (`packages/core/src/worker/auth.ts`, set on `c.var.worker`).
- The send route already resolves the opaque handle to `channelKey` + `threadId` (`routes/internal/conversations.ts:160-180`). Handles are opaque base64url `c_`/`t_`, so this comparison can only happen server-side — the worker can't do it.
- The terminal payload already carries turn-scoped facts the bridge reads: `toolsUsed` is the exact precedent (`core/src/types.ts:284`, stamped at `gateway-integration.ts:220`).
- There's already a plugin→worker callback for "this tool did something the turn must know about": `onAskUserPosted` (`plugin-conversations/src/index.ts:15` → `session-runner.ts:1219`).

So: send route compares resolved conversation against `worker.conversationId` and returns `deliveredInBand: true`; the plugin fires a callback; the transport stamps one boolean on the terminal row; the bridge skips `handleCompletion` when it's set. No new table, no cross-pod state, no second lock — the payload is the carrier, same as `toolsUsed`.

**On #4** — nothing to fix. No product code hardcodes an org slug; every Lobu URL resolves it at runtime via `getOrganizationSlug`. The only `lobu-crm` hits are docs, `examples/`, and test fixtures. Old Slack messages carrying `/lobu-crm/...` links are dead, but that's stored history, not code.

One genuine product call is yours:

<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. @AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

On 2026-07-28 a concurrent agent/automation on this machine twice destroyed in-flight work in `.claude/worktrees/`: first it deleted the whole `activity-memory-split` worktree (uncommitted owletto changes lost, reconstructed from conversation context), later it gutted the recreated worktree down to `packages/owletto` and de-registered it (`git worktree list` no longer showed it; git commands inside fell through to the MAIN checkout — which it left sitting on a feature branch). Disk was also at 99% with the automation re-installing node_modules in worktrees as fast as caches were cleared.

**Why:** worktrees are shared mutable state between sessions; a cleanup/bump job prunes what looks stale, and uncommitted submodule changes don't make the outer worktree look dirty.

**How to apply:**
- In a submodule worktree, `git commit` + `git push -u origin <branch>` as soon as a coherent chunk exists — BEFORE running long gates. Pushed commits survived both wipes; working trees did not.
- If a worktree's git commands start reporting main-repo branches/paths, STOP — the worktree is orphaned and every git command is hitting `~/Code/lobu`.
- Recovery trick: a plain `git clone --reference-if-able ~/Code/lobu/.git/modules/packages/owletto` dropped into `packages/owletto` works fine in place of the submodule; and symlinking the worktree-root `node_modules` to the main checkout's resolves the workspace deps without a 2GB install.
- Disk full on this box: safe reclaims are worktree `node_modules`/`dist`, `~/.bun/install/cache`, `~/Library/Caches/{bun,ms-playwright,org.swift.swiftpm}`.

content.text:
Yes — exactly right on all three cases. To be precise about the semantics I'm building:

- **Agent posts nothing** → flag never set → bridge delivers `finalText` to Slack exactly as today. Unchanged path.
- **Agent posts 1..N messages into the triggering conversation** → the flag is a one-way latch, so any number of posts is fine; the terminal reply is suppressed once.
- **Agent posts only to a *different* conversation** (you said "post this to #general") → not in-band → `finalText` still gets delivered to the triggering conversation, so you still get "done, posted it".
- **Mixed** (posts to #general *and* answers you in the DM) → latch set → terminal suppressed, because it already answered you.

Your question surfaced one edge I need to get right: the flag must ride `signalCompletion` only, **not** `signalError` — an error is not a duplicate of the reply, so a turn that posts in-band and then fails must still surface the error. Building it that way.

name: reference_worktree_submodule_drift_fails_pre_pr
description: A stale packages/owletto checkout in a task worktree fails make pre-pr with a frontend tsc error that CI will never see
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: 9b2cbf0b-681a-45b4-93cf-d91a16522d4c

---

`make pre-pr` builds the **checked-out** `packages/owletto`, not the SHA the branch pins. In a worktree that has been alive a while, `make task-setup` leaves the submodule on a per-task branch that drifts, so pre-pr fails with a frontend error in a file the PR never touched.

Seen 2026-07-30 on PR #2340 (3 server files, zero frontend):

```
src/components/agents/skill-editor.tsx(35,26): error TS2339:
  Property 'nixPackages' does not exist on type ...
make: *** [pre-pr] Error 2
```

**Diagnose before fixing anything** — the failure is real output, but it may be local-only:

```
git submodule status packages/owletto     # leading '+' = working tree != pinned SHA
git ls-tree HEAD packages/owletto         # what my branch pins
git ls-tree origin/main packages/owletto  # what main pins
```

If HEAD and `origin/main` pin the **same** SHA and the PR touches no frontend, the error cannot reach CI — CI checks out the pin. Fix locally:

```
cd packages/owletto && git fetch -q origin && git checkout <pinned-sha>
```

- Slack sent **two** messages per agent turn: the agent's real answer (posted mid-run via the `send_message` conversation tool) and then the run's terminal `finalText` — a past-tense report about that answer — delivered again by `chat-response-bridge`, carrying the `View in Lobu ↗` footer. Observed in prod DM `D095U1QV667` on 2026-07-30 and 2026-07-27.
- Suppress the terminal delivery **only** when the agent already answered *in this conversation*. The rule is structural, not semantic — we never try to classify "is this text a summary". `/internal/conversations/send` resolves the model's opaque handle to concrete channel/thread coordinates and compares them against the run's own conversation from the **signed worker token**; the worker latches that fact and stamps `repliedInBand` on the terminal completion row, exactly as it already stamps `toolsUsed`. No new table, no cross-pod state, no second lock.
- Delete the `View in Lobu ↗` footer entirely (#2137). The per-turn run-context block (#2322) already hands the agent the conversation URL, so it can produce a link when asked.

Behavior matrix:

| Agent posted | Terminal reply |
|---|---|
| nothing | delivered (unchanged) |
| 1..N times into the triggering conversation | **suppressed** (latch) |
| only into a *different* conversation (e.g. `#general`) | delivered — the answer here is still owed |
| into `#general` **and** here | suppressed |

Fails **open** in every ambiguous case: an absent flag (older worker, nothing posted, unparseable id, thread mismatch) always delivers. ---
name: project_chat_inband_reply_dedupe
description: "PR #2403 — Slack double-posted every agent turn (in-band answer + terminal summary); structural fix via repliedInBand stamp, and the View in Lobu footer was deleted"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

Slack sent **two** messages per agent turn, seen in prod DM `D095U1QV667`
(2026-07-30, 2026-07-27): the agent's real answer posted mid-run via the
`send_message` conversation tool, then the run's terminal `finalText` — a
past-tense report about that answer ("Selamını yanıtladım ✅") — delivered again
by `chat-response-bridge`, carrying the `View in Lobu ↗` footer.

**The rule is structural, never semantic.** Do not try to classify "is this text
a summary". The decidable fact is: *did the agent already post into the run's own
conversation?* If it posted to a DIFFERENT channel (user said "post to #general")
the terminal reply is still owed and must be delivered.

Mechanism (PR #2403, 15 files, no new table / lock / cross-pod state):
- `/internal/conversations/send` resolves the model's OPAQUE handle (`c_`/`t_`
  base64url) to channel+thread coords and compares against the run's own
  conversation from the **signed worker token** (`WorkerTokenData.conversationId`).
  Only the route can do this — the worker never sees channel ids it wasn't given.
- Worker latches it and stamps `repliedInBand` on the terminal completion row,
  exactly as it already stamps `toolsUsed` (`gateway-integration.ts`). The
  payload is the carrier, so it is replica-safe for the same reason `finalText` is.
- Stamped in `signalCompletion` ONLY, never `signalError` — an error is not a
  duplicate of the reply and must always surface.
- Fails OPEN: absent flag (old worker, nothing posted, unparseable id, thread
  mismatch) always delivers. Suppression needs a positive exact match.

`parseConversationRef` exists because a top-level Slack DM arrives as
`slack:D0123:` with an EMPTY trailing segment — a naive `===` against the channel
form reports a false mismatch and lets the double-post through for every DM.

Also in this PR: the `View in Lobu ↗` footer (#2137) DELETED entirely — the
per-turn run-context block (#2322) already gives the agent the conversation URL.
`review-fix` caught two misses: a suppressed reply was still written to the
durable channel transcript (phantom bot message) and still generated chips.

**Known gaps:** live-streaming platforms (Telegram) still stream the narration as
deltas before the completion, so the fix is complete only for post-once (Slack).
Telegram forum-topic in-band posts don't match (thread root is a message id vs
the topic id) — fail-open, untested. The send route's computation has no test
(needs Postgres; none local).

**BLOCKED ON MERGE by `check-drift`**, which is repo-wide and NOT caused by this
PR: `owletto/main` is 2 commits ahead (#671, #672) of the pinned SHA and no
parent bump PR exists. Every PR is blocked until someone bumps the pointer —
which ships those two frontend PRs, so it is a product call.

Related: [[reference_agent_run_context_and_lobu_urls]],
[[reference_behavior_execution_writes_two_runs]], [[project_conversation_tools_pr]].

On 2026-07-28 a concurrent agent/automation on this machine twice destroyed in-flight work in `.claude/worktrees/`: first it deleted the whole `activity-memory-split` worktree (uncommitted owletto changes lost, reconstructed from conversation context), later it gutted the recreated worktree down to `packages/owletto` and de-registered it (`git worktree list` no longer showed it; git commands inside fell through to the MAIN checkout — which it left sitting on a feature branch). - Disk full on this box: safe reclaims are worktree `node_modules`/`dist`, `~/.bun/install/cache`, `~/Library/Caches/{bun,ms-playwright,org.swift.swiftpm}`.

Done and pushed. **PR #2403** — review verdict `bugs 0, 0 blockers, tests_adequate: true`.

## What changed

```
packages/server/src/gateway/routes/internal/conversations.ts   |  18 ++   ← decides in-band
packages/server/src/gateway/conversations/conversation-ref.ts  |  56 ++   ← new, comparison

packages/server/.../lobu-answer-link.ts                        |  56 --   ← DELETED
+ 3 worker wiring files, 4 test files
15 files, +346 / −380
```

Answering your question directly: **no summary is ever classified.** The decidable fact is whether the agent already posted into *this* conversation. The send route resolves the model's opaque handle to real channel/thread coords and compares against the run's conversation from the signed worker token; the worker latches that and stamps `repliedInBand` on the terminal row, riding the same carrier as the existing `toolsUsed`. No new table, no lock, no cross-pod state. It fails **open** — an absent flag always delivers, so suppression needs a positive exact match.

Your mid-flight question caught a real edge: the flag rides `signalCompletion` only, never `signalError`, so a turn that answers in-band and then fails still surfaces the error.

## Evidence

Red→green, with the red produced by mutating the one decision line to `false` (doubling as the mutation test):

```
RED:   Expected number of calls: 0 / Received number of calls: 1   → 29 pass, 1 fail
GREEN: 41 pass, 0 fail
```

`make review-fix` (via `REVIEWER_CLI=claude` — codex is quota-blocked to Aug 5) caught two things I missed: the suppressed reply was still written to the durable channel transcript as a phantom bot message, and still generated suggest-action chips. Both fixed and verified.

## Confidence

- **Suppression logic + comparison — 90.** Red→green reproducer, 11 unit cases including the `slack:D0123:` trailing-colon DM form that a naive `===` gets wrong, plus an independent reviewer pass. CI `unit` and `typecheck` both green.
- **End-to-end in prod Slack — 35.** Never booted. No local Postgres (`pg_isready` fails), so the send route's in-band computation — the one place the decision is actually made — has zero test coverage. I verified the wiring by reading it, not by running it.
- **Footer removal — 95.** Module and its last consumer deleted, no dangling references, knip clean.

## Two things blocking / worth knowing

**`check-drift` fails, and it isn't mine.** `owletto/main` is 2 commits ahead (#671, #672) of the pinned SHA with no parent bump PR. My branch pins the *identical* SHA as `origin/main`, so main fails this check right now too — every PR is blocked. Bumping it ships those two frontend PRs, which is your call, not a side effect I should slip into a bug fix.

**Your worktrees are being destroyed mid-session.** `make task-setup` reported success and the tree was gone seconds later; I lost six files of edits and replayed them. Disk is at 97% (13Gi free). This is the second recorded occurrence.

1. Decide on the owletto pointer bump — it unblocks #2403 and every other PR, but ships #671/#672.
2. Once merged, verify live in that DM: one message, no footer. That's the 35 → high step.
3. Look at whatever is pruning `.claude/worktrees/` and reclaim disk.
4. Optional one-liner: `exec-sandbox-extra.test.ts` asserts an error string the source no longer emits — fails on macOS, invisible on CI's Linux runners. Left out of scope.

# Count commits on $branch that aren't reachable from $upstream. Echoes 0 when
# $upstream is missing (treats "no upstream" as "no proven publish"; caller
# may still bail elsewhere). Echoes a positive number if the branch is ahead.
ahead_of() {
  local gitdir="$1" upstream="$2"
  if ! git -C "$gitdir" rev-parse --verify "$upstream" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

content.text:
CI is settling in the background. Here's where the other two landed.

## 1. Owletto bump — resolved without a new PR

Someone bumped it while I was working. `origin/main` now pins `89dddbdb` with **zero** non-bot commits past it. I rebased #2403 onto it; `check-drift` now **passes**, and so do `unit`, `frontend`, `migrations`, `format-lint`, `base-branch-guard`. `typecheck` and `integration` were still running. File list is still exactly the intended 15.

## 3. The worktree wipes

Not a scheduler — no cron, no launchd job. The mechanism is `scripts/task-clean.sh`: it refuses to delete a worktree with uncommitted changes or unpushed commits, **but `--force` / `FORCE=1` skips every one of those guards**. Combined with the disk at 97%, the likely story is another session force-cleaning to reclaim space — which matches my earlier note that the box was at 99% with automation reinstalling `node_modules` as fast as caches were cleared.

Reclaimed ~1G of dev caches (bun install cache, bun, typescript — all re-downloadable). I stopped there deliberately: the real weight is **~14G across 8 worktrees, and every one has live work** (dirty and/or ahead of `origin/main`). Deleting their `node_modules` would do to someone else exactly what was done to me. The remaining big items are your app caches (Spotify 3.5G, Google 3.4G, WhatsApp 858M) — your call, not mine to delete.

The durable fix is structural: worktrees each carry a private 1.9G `node_modules`. Symlinking them to the main checkout's resolves workspace deps without the per-worktree install, which is a change to `task-setup.sh` and your decision.

## Ambient mode — the mechanism exists, but only per-Behavior

`NO_REPLY` is a red herring. It's wired **only** into the memory-flush prompt ("Reply with NO_REPLY if nothing to store") and consumed at `worker.ts:531` purely to log `no_reply` vs `stored`. It has never touched chat delivery.

What does exist is `trigger.output`, an enum of exactly two values, defaulting to `silent`:

```
output: "silent" | "reply_to_source"     // default "silent"
```

`activation.ts:65` routes on it: `reply_to_source` → `replyTargets` (answers through the chat transport); anything else → `backgroundTargets` (writes a run row, posts nothing). **So ambient mode already works — that's the default.** A `silent` Behavior watching a channel already says nothing, no matter what the model produces.

The real gap is a **per-turn** decision. Inside a `reply_to_source` turn, the agent cannot choose to stay quiet — its terminal text is always delivered. Today the only lever is emitting empty text, which models essentially never do; they write "No action needed" and that gets posted.

**My recommendation: a third `output` mode where silence is the default and speech is the explicit act.** Under it the bridge always suppresses the terminal reply, and `send_message` becomes the only channel to the user.

I'd pick this over the two alternatives:

- A `NO_REPLY` sentinel for chat is the cheap option, but it puts a text matcher at a delivery boundary — `NO_REPLY.` with a period fails open, a reply that quotes the token fails closed, and nothing is auditable. Your own AGENTS.md rule against text matchers as boundaries applies exactly here.
- A `skip_reply` tool is structurally sound but spends a tool slot in every chat agent's prompt to express a *negative*, and it only helps if the model remembers to call it.

The third mode needs no new sentinel, no new tool, and no new mechanism — it reuses the `repliedInBand` suppression this PR just built, simply always-on instead of conditional. It also inverts the failure direction correctly: a rambling model produces silence rather than channel noise, and the channel shows exactly what the agent chose to say. Cost is one extra tool round-trip per reply, and the enum already exists so it's a small typed addition rather than new machinery.

**Confidence:** high (90) that `trigger.output` is the ambient switch and that `NO_REPLY` is unrelated to chat delivery — read the schema, the routing branch, and every call site. The recommendation itself is a design judgment, not a verified claim.

**Next:** I'll merge #2403 when CI reports green, then the live check in that DM is still owed — that's the one thing separating "tests pass" from "verified in prod". Want me to spec the third `output` mode as a follow-up PR?

# Tool-surface eval — glm-4.7

Empirical comparison of two ways to expose Lobu's MCP tools to an agent model,
run against the **real glm-4.7 model via the z-ai provider**:

- **Arm A — discrete MCP** (`mcpExposure: "tools"`, the default cloud surface):
  all ~23 Lobu MCP tools are first-class function-call tools.
- **Arm B — just-bash / MCP-as-CLI** (`mcpExposure: "cli"`, the embedded
  deployment surface): one `bash` tool, and the MCP tools are reachable as
  `lobu <tool> <<<'{json}'`, discoverable via `lobu --help` and
  `lobu <tool> --schema`.

The toggle that selects between them in production is the worker's
`mcpExposure` (set per-agent via `toolsConfig.mcpExposure` or the
`LOBU_MCP_EXPOSURE=cli` env var) — see
`packages/agent-worker/src/runtime/worker.ts`.

## What is real vs. reconstructed

- **Model:** real glm-4.7 over z-ai (`Z_AI_API_KEY`), model object built exactly
  as the worker's `model-resolver.ts` does (openai-completions, base URL
  `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`, `compat.supportsStore=false`).
- **Tools:** the REAL Lobu MCP handlers (`manage_entity`, `save_memory`,
  `search_memory`, `query_sql`, `manage_behaviors`, …) against a real Postgres
  (the server package's test fixtures + migrations on `lobu_test`).
- **Arm A surface:** the real discrete tool list from
  `getAllTools()` (names/descriptions/JSON schemas).
- **Arm B surface:** the real `buildMcpCliCommands` + the worker's real
  `createLobuTools` bash + just-bash interpreter. The only swap is the
  gateway HTTP `callTool` → an out-of-process dispatcher (see below).

content.text:
Both watchers running. Let me answer your first question properly while they finish.

## What the "output mode" thing is

It's an existing field on every Behavior's trigger — a two-value enum, defaulting to `silent`:

```ts
// packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-behaviors.ts:53
output: Type.Union([Type.Literal("silent"), Type.Literal("reply_to_source")], {
  description: "Keep the result in Lobu or send it back through the source connector when supported.",
  default: "silent",
})
```

`packages/server/src/behaviors/activation.ts:65` routes on it:

```ts
if ((trigger.execution ?? "turn") === "turn" &&
    (trigger.output ?? "silent") === "reply_to_source") {
  replyTargets.push(match)      // answers through the chat transport
} else {
  backgroundTargets.push(match) // writes a run row, posts nothing
}
```

So there are already two worlds. A `silent` Behavior watching a channel runs on every matching message, does its work, writes a run row, and **nothing reaches Slack no matter what the model says**. That's ambient, and it already works — it's the default.

`reply_to_source` is the other world: the terminal text *is* the reply. And that's where the gap is. Inside a `reply_to_source` turn there is no per-turn choice — whatever the model produces gets posted. The only lever today is emitting empty text, which models don't do. `NO_REPLY` is not a fallback here; it's wired solely into the memory-flush prompt and consumed at `worker.ts:531` just to log `no_reply` vs `stored`.

So the design question is genuinely: **what's the third mode**, for an agent that's in the channel and allowed to speak but should usually stay quiet.

## Early spike signal (1 trial, uncorrected — treat as directional only)

The most interesting result is *why* the sentinel failed. Told "reply with exactly NO_REPLY if you have nothing to add," glm-5.2 instead wrote:

> "Nothing actionable here — just a casual acknowledgment from Sarah in #sales. No action needed on my end."

> "This looks like a message between Mike and Dave that doesn't involve me — no action needed on my end."

That's the exact third-person narration that caused your original double-post — the model narrates its decision rather than emitting a control token. That's a mechanism failure, not a judgment failure, and it's the strongest argument against the sentinel: it fails on the very behavior it's meant to suppress.

I also caught a harness bug mid-flight worth flagging, because it was inflating results in two arms: the model sometimes calls `send_message` with **null text**. I was counting that as a delivery; production 400s it (`if (!body?.target || !text)`). Corrected to count those as fumbles, and the 3-trial run is re-running now. I'll give you real numbers rather than the noisy first pass.

## Status

- **#2403 merged** (`63ba9442`) — all 8 required checks green including `integration`, `pi-review` re-run clean on the rebased HEAD (`bugs 0, slop 0, 0 blockers`).
- **Not yet in prod.** Deployed revision is `6941929b2`, which predates the merge. Watcher is now polling correctly.

**Confidence:** high (95) on the output-mode explanation — read the schema, the routing branch, and every call site. Low (30) on the spike numbers so far; 1 trial with a counting bug is not a result, which is why it's re-running.

**Next:** when the corrected spike lands I'll give you the false-post / false-silence table per arm, and when prod picks up the merge I'll send a DM in that Slack thread and confirm one message instead of two. I have Slack MCP access so I can verify it directly rather than via the browser — the browser would only show the Lobu-side transcript, not what Slack actually rendered.

name: feedback-concurrent-agent-worktree-wipe
description: Concurrent automation deletes/guts worktrees + submodule checkouts; commit+push the submodule BEFORE any long verification
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 830d2806-d323-48b7-80b9-f28cf7556caf
  modified: 2026-07-31T14:43:47.865Z
---

On 2026-07-28 a concurrent agent/automation on this machine twice destroyed in-flight work in `.claude/worktrees/`: first it deleted the whole `activity-memory-split` worktree (uncommitted owletto changes lost, reconstructed from conversation context), later it gutted the recreated worktree down to `packages/owletto` and de-registered it (`git worktree list` no longer showed it; git commands inside fell through to the MAIN checkout — which it left sitting on a feature branch). Disk was also at 99% with the automation re-installing node_modules in worktrees as fast as caches were cleared.

**Why:** worktrees are shared mutable state between sessions; a cleanup/bump job prunes what looks stale, and uncommitted submodule changes don't make the outer worktree look dirty.

**Recurred 2026-07-31** (session on PR #2403), same signature, disk again at 97%: `make task-setup` reported success and the worktree was destroyed within *seconds* — the first `Edit` after it failed with "File does not exist", and `git worktree list` showed it `prunable`. Uncommitted edits to 6 files were lost and had to be replayed from conversation context. A second recreate survived only because every edit was applied and committed in ONE shell invocation. Other worktrees also vanished between two consecutive `git worktree list` calls in the same session. Main checkout stayed clean — the edits did NOT leak there.

**How to apply:**
- In a submodule worktree, `git commit` + `git push -u origin <branch>` as soon as a coherent chunk exists — BEFORE running long gates. Pushed commits survived both wipes; working trees did not.
- When the box is in this state, batch worktree creation + ALL edits + commit + push into a single Bash call. Per-edit round-trips are what lose the work. A heredoc'd python script doing exact-match substitutions (asserting each match count) replays a whole change set atomically.
- If a worktree's git commands start reporting main-repo branches/paths, STOP — the worktree is orphaned and every git command is hitting `~/Code/lobu`.
- Recovery trick: a plain `git clone --reference-if-able ~/Code/lobu/.git/modules/packages/owletto` dropped into `packages/owletto` works fine in place of the submodule; and symlinking the worktree-root `node_modules` to the main checkout's resolves the workspace deps without a 2GB install.
- Disk full on this box: safe reclaims are worktree `node_modules`/`dist`, `~/.bun/install/cache`, `~/Library/Caches/{bun,ms-playwright,org.swift.swiftpm}`.

---
name: project_chat_inband_reply_dedupe
description: "PR #2403 — Slack double-posted every agent turn (in-band answer + terminal summary); structural fix via repliedInBand stamp, and the View in Lobu footer was deleted"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1b95a027-7948-46dc-8553-ddfe89bc6524
  modified: 2026-07-31T14:43:37.373Z
---

Slack sent **two** messages per agent turn, seen in prod DM `D095U1QV667`
(2026-07-30, 2026-07-27): the agent's real answer posted mid-run via the
`send_message` conversation tool, then the run's terminal `finalText` — a
past-tense report about that answer ("Selamını yanıtladım ✅") — delivered again
by `chat-response-bridge`, carrying the `View in Lobu ↗` footer.

**The rule is structural, never semantic.** Do not try to classify "is this text
a summary". The decidable fact is: *did the agent already post into the run's own
conversation?* If it posted to a DIFFERENT channel (user said "post to #general")
the terminal reply is still owed and must be delivered.

Mechanism (PR #2403, 15 files, no new table / lock / cross-pod state):
- `/internal/conversations/send` resolves the model's OPAQUE handle (`c_`/`t_`
  base64url) to channel+thread coords and compares against the run's own
  conversation from the **signed worker token** (`WorkerTokenData.conversationId`).
  Only the route can do this — the worker never sees channel ids it wasn't given.
- Worker latches it and stamps `repliedInBand` on the terminal completion row,
  exactly as it already stamps `toolsUsed` (`gateway-integration.ts`). The
  payload is the carrier, so it is replica-safe for the same reason `finalText` is.
- Stamped in `signalCompletion` ONLY, never `signalError` — an error is not a
  duplicate of the reply and must always surface.
- Fails OPEN: absent flag (old worker, nothing posted, unparseable id, thread
  mismatch) always delivers. Suppression needs a positive exact match.

`parseConversationRef` exists because a top-level Slack DM arrives as
`slack:D0123:` with an EMPTY trailing segment — a naive `===` against the channel
form reports a false mismatch and lets the double-post through for every DM.

Also in this PR: the `View in Lobu ↗` footer (#2137) DELETED entirely — the
per-turn run-context block (#2322) already gives the agent the conversation URL.
`review-fix` caught two misses: a suppressed reply was still written to the
durable channel transcript (phantom bot message) and still generated chips.

**Known gaps:** live-streaming platforms (Telegram) still stream the narration as
deltas before the completion, so the fix is complete only for post-once (Slack).
Telegram forum-topic in-band posts don't match (thread root is a message id vs
the topic id) — fail-open, untested. The send route's computation has no test
(needs Postgres; none local).

**BLOCKED ON MERGE by `check-drift`**, which is repo-wide and NOT caused by this
PR: `owletto/main` is 2 commits ahead (#671, #672) of the pinned SHA and no
parent bump PR exists. Every PR is blocked until someone bumps the pointer —
which ships those two frontend PRs, so it is a product call.

Related: [[reference_agent_run_context_and_lobu_urls]],
[[reference_behavior_execution_writes_two_runs]], [[project_conversation_tools_pr]].

content.text:
**#2403 is done and confirmed live.** Here's where things stand while the spike finishes.

## Prod verification (the thing that was owed)

Real A/B in your DM, same prompt both times, only the deployed code differing:

- **Before** — 2 messages: the answer, then 6s later "E2e kontrolünü yanıtladım — ayakta olduğumu teyit ettim." + `View in Lobu ↗`
- **After** — 1 message: "Buradayım ✅ CRM ajanı çalışıyor, komut bekliyorum."

Re-read the channel a minute later to rule out a delayed second post. Still one. Memory updated with the merge SHA and the A/B.

Two caveats I want to be straight about rather than let the green result imply more than it proves. This tested the **suppression** direction — agent posts in-band, terminal narration gets dropped. It did **not** exercise the fallback direction, where the agent never calls `send_message` and the terminal text is the only reply; that path relies on unit tests plus the fail-open design (suppression requires a positive server-side coordinate match, so silence can only follow a send the user already saw). And the **Telegram gap is untouched** — live-streaming platforms push the narration as deltas before completion ever happens, so there's nothing to suppress. The fix is complete for post-once platforms only.

## On the spike

Still running — 72 real model calls, and the command pipes through `tail -22` so it stays silent until it exits. I'll report the full table when it lands.

One thing I can already say without the numbers, because it's mechanism rather than measurement: **#2403 has quietly made arm I cheap to build.** The inverted design ("terminal text is scratch space, `send_message` is the only way to speak") needs exactly the plumbing I just shipped — the server-side coordinate match that decides whether a post landed in the run's own conversation. A third `output` mode would mostly be flipping the default rather than new infrastructure.

The sentinel arm is the one I expect the data to kill, and for a reason worth more than its score: in the smoke run glm-5.2 responded to "reply with exactly NO_REPLY" by *narrating its decision to stay quiet* — "Nothing actionable here — just a casual acknowledgment from Sarah in #sales." That's the identical failure shape as the bug you reported. A mechanism that fails by producing the exact artifact it exists to prevent is a bad mechanism regardless of its hit rate.

**Confidence: 95 on the prod fix** — direct before/after in the real channel, not a log or a typecheck. **~40 on the silence recommendation** so far; the mechanism argument is solid but I have one noisy trial, and I'd rather hand you three clean ones.

**Next, once the spike reports:**
1. Full falsePost / falseSilence / doublePost / fumbledSends table per arm, with the recommendation.
2. If arm I wins as expected, spec the third `trigger.output` mode as a follow-up PR.
3. Telegram streaming gap — the remaining half of the double-post problem, currently unaddressed.
4. Optional: a `reply_to_source` turn where the agent doesn't post in-band, to close the fallback-direction gap empirically.

content.text:
Yes — and I think your instinct is right, but it splits into two halves that want *different* mechanisms. First, the spike: I have to throw it out.

## The spike is invalid

`falseSilence 12/12` in all three arms is the tell — no arm ever delivered anything, which can't be a real behavioral difference. Two harness bugs, both mine:

pi's tool contract is `execute(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate)`. I wrote `execute: async (a: {text}) => …`, so `a` was the **tool-call id string** and `a.text` was always `undefined`. Every `send_message` got scored as a fumble (hence `fumbledSends` 20/10/17) and `sent` was empty in every cell. Separately, my `finalText` extraction breaks on the last assistant message even when it's tool-calls-only with no text block, so terminal text read as `""` everywhere. Delivery was structurally pinned to zero in all arms. It measured nothing — ignore the earlier 1-trial numbers too, same defect.

## The design question, which doesn't depend on it

Grepping the ingest path turned up something that changes the shape of this: **the addressed/unaddressed bit already exists and is already plumbed through.**

`message-handler-bridge.ts:601` classifies every inbound message as `source: "mention" | "dm" | "subscribed"`, and carries it forward as `is_mention`/`mention_only` event attributes (`:701`) and `isDirect` (`:1250`). So "was the bot tagged" is a decidable structural fact available at run time — no model judgment, nothing to build. That's your first half, free.

Your second half — "if not tagged and there's a confidence interval" — is where I'd push back slightly, on the *knob*, not the goal. Self-reported LLM confidence is badly calibrated: models cluster their own numbers, and you can't tune a threshold without labelled per-channel data you don't have. It also re-introduces the semantic-classification approach that #2403 deliberately avoided.

The reframe I'd suggest: don't ask the model how confident it is. Change **which direction forgetting fails**, per branch.

- **Addressed** (`mention`/`dm`) → terminal text is delivered, suppression forbidden. Fails toward speech, because false silence is the harm when someone asked directly.
- **Ambient** (`subscribed`) → terminal text is *never* delivered; `send_message` is the only way to speak. Fails toward silence, because false posting is the harm.

One already-computed bit picks the fail direction. The value is that in the ambient branch, speaking becomes an **affirmative act** rather than a suppression — so the dominant LLM failure mode, forgetting the instruction, produces silence in exactly the branch where silence is correct most of the time. Sentinels and skip-tools both invert that: forgetting produces a post, which is your original bug. And this is the branch #2403 already built the plumbing for.

One thing worth flagging that you didn't ask about: **cadence is a separate axis from judgment.** A bot with perfect judgment that chimes in on 30% of messages still reads as noisy — humans self-throttle in channels. `min_cooldown_seconds` already exists (`packages/server/src/behaviors/cooldown.ts`), though my note says it's event-trigger-only, so whether it covers this path needs checking rather than assuming.

**Confidence:** high (90) that the addressed-bit exists and is plumbed — read the classification, the attributes, and the propagation. Medium (60) on the fail-direction recommendation: the mechanism argument is strong and matches the one real datapoint we have (your actual Slack double-post), but I have **no** valid empirical support, and I'm not going to pretend the spike gave me any. Low on cooldown coverage — grepped that the field exists, didn't trace it.

**Next:**
1. Fix the two harness bugs and re-run — it's a ~10 min turnaround and would give the recommendation actual support.
2. Trace whether `min_cooldown_seconds` applies to chat-triggered runs or only event ones.
3. If you'd rather skip the spike, spec the third `output` mode directly — the design above is buildable now.
4. Telegram streaming gap still open: it posts narration as deltas before completion, so #2403 can't suppress it there.

import type { DbClient } from "../db/client";
import { getDb } from "../db/client";
import logger from "../utils/logger";

/**
 * `watchers.min_cooldown_seconds` debounce for event-triggered Behaviors.
 *
 * A Behavior activates on an event through two substrates: background targets
 * become durable `behavior` runs via `createBehaviorEventRun`, and
 * `reply_to_source` targets are handed to the chat transport and never write a
 * run row at all. A predicate over `runs` would therefore be a silent no-op on
 * exactly one half of the feature, so both paths claim the same cursor
 * (`watchers.last_event_activation_at`) through this module.
 *
 * The claim must be serialized, or two concurrent deliveries both read "no
 * recent activation" and both fire. It reuses the advisory lock
 * `createBehaviorEventRun` already takes per Behavior rather than introducing
 * a second one: the lock is transaction-scoped, so the read and the cursor
 * write cannot interleave with another replica's.
 */
const BEHAVIOR_ACTIVATION_LOCK_NAMESPACE = "behavior_event_run";

/**
 * Serialize activation decisions for one Behavior. Transaction-scoped: the
 * lock is released when `tx` commits or rolls back.
 */
export async function lockBehaviorForActivation(
  tx: DbClient,
  watcherId: number,
): Promise<void> {
  await tx`
    SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(
      hashtext(${BEHAVIOR_ACTIVATION_LOCK_NAMESPACE}),
      ${watcherId}
    )
  `;
}

/**
 * Consume this Behavior's cooldown window, returning whether the activation
 * may proceed. Callers MUST already hold `lockBehaviorForActivation` on the
 * same transaction — the read and the write below are only atomic together.
 *
 * A Behavior with `min_cooldown_seconds = 0` (the NOT NULL default) is always
 * allowed and never writes the cursor, so the common path costs one indexed
 * read and no row contention.
 *
 * Returns false for a Behavior that no longer exists: a deleted Behavior has
 * nothing to activate.
 */

content.text:
All three checked against the code. Two confirmed, and **one of them proves I told you something wrong**.

## 1. Spike harness — confirmed broken, three bugs

`AgentTool.execute` is `(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate)` (`pi-agent-core/dist/types.d.ts:304`). My spike read `.text` off argument 0, which is the **tool-call id string** — so `params.text` was undefined on every call, every send scored as a fumble, `sent` was empty in all 72 cells. Second bug: the result shape is `{content:[{type:"text",text}], details:{}}`, not `{output}`. Third: my `finalText` reader broke on the last assistant message even when it was tool-calls-only with no text block, so terminal text read as `""` everywhere. Delivery was pinned to zero in all three arms by construction — that's the `12/12` across the board. All three fixed; corrected run is going now.

Worth noting the third bug only surfaced when I symlinked `node_modules` into the scratchpad, which silently changed module resolution (`setTools` vanished). I reverted to the original resolution rather than leave that variable in.

## 2. Cooldown — I was wrong, it already covers chat

I told you `min_cooldown_seconds` was "event-trigger-only, needs checking." It isn't. `message-handler-bridge.ts:1185` claims it for `reply_to_source` targets too, and the comment says it was wired deliberately for exactly this reason:

> `reply_to_source` Behaviors answer through the chat transport and never write a `behavior` run row, so they are invisible to the cooldown claim `createBehaviorEventRun` makes for background targets above. Claiming the same cursor here is what stops `min_cooldown_seconds` being a debounce on one half of the feature and a silent no-op on the other.

So cadence control exists for both halves already. But there's a real limitation for ambient use: the cursor is `watchers.last_event_activation_at`, a column on the **Behavior** row — so it's per-Behavior and global across channels, not per-conversation. A bot watching five channels that speaks in `#sales` goes mute in `#eng` for the whole window. For ambient mode you'd almost certainly want the debounce keyed per conversation, which is a schema change, not a config one.

## 3. Telegram gap — confirmed

`deliversAtCompletion` defaults to `false` (`platform-strategies/index.ts:42`); only Slack overrides it to `true` (`slack.ts:181`). The `repliedInBand` suppression hangs off `strategy.deliversAtCompletion` at `chat-response-bridge.ts:394/438`, so on streaming platforms the narration is already out as deltas before completion is reached. Nothing to suppress. #2403 is genuinely Slack-only.

## What this means for the ambient design

The fail-direction model you agreed to holds, and the confirmations tighten it: the addressed bit exists, and cadence exists. The two real gaps are the **per-Behavior cooldown scope** and **streaming platforms**, and the second one bites harder — an ambient mode built on "terminal text is never delivered" is only enforceable where delivery happens at completion. On Telegram the text is already streaming out, so ambient mode there needs suppression at the *stream* layer, not the completion layer. That's a bigger change than the Slack path and worth knowing before scoping.

**Confidence:** high (95) on all three confirmations — each read from source, not inferred. The cooldown correction in particular is quoted from the code comment.

**Next:**
1. Report the corrected spike numbers when it lands (running now) — the first thing that'll give the fail-direction model actual support rather than just mechanism.
2. Decide ambient scope: Slack-only first, or solve the streaming layer too. My read is Slack-first, since that's where you're feeling the pain and where the plumbing already exists.
3. Per-conversation cooldown keying — needed for ambient, but separable from the output mode.
4. I'll update the memory note that wrongly says cooldown is event-only.

description: "min_cooldown_seconds was inert; wired to the EVENT path (which INCLUDES chat reply_to_source) but NOT the cron path, which would hot-loop. Cursor is per-Behavior, not per-conversation."

`watchers.min_cooldown_seconds` (`NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`) was stored, surfaced in the MCP contract, `defineBehavior` (`packages/cli/src/config/define.ts:432`), `lobu apply`/`init-from-org`, and the table schema — and read by **no dispatch predicate**. Same dead-config class as `permission_mode`. PR #2341 (2026-07-30) wires it.

**Wired to the EVENT path only** (`behaviors/activation.ts:findMatchingBehaviorActivations`), deliberately:
- cron already spaces scheduled firings, so a cooldown there is redundant;
- worse, it would be a hot loop. The scheduled path would skip materializing a run, but `next_run_at` only advances when a run reaches a terminal state (`advanceWatcherSchedule`). A suppressed scheduled firing leaves the cursor in the past and the Behavior re-selects every tick — exactly what #2326 fixed. Making it safe needs cursor-advance-on-suppression, i.e. new mechanism to argue termination → the coordination design brake says move the check, not add mechanism.
- event activations have no cursor to strand.

There are **two independent firing paths** — `materializeDueWatcherRuns` (schedule, `automation.ts:761`) and `findMatchingBehaviorActivations` (event, `activation.ts:101`). Any Behavior-wide gating change must consider both or it is an instance fix.

Implementation notes: counts ANY firing (not just `completed`), else a burst is only debounced after the first run happens to finish. The `min_cooldown_seconds = 0` arm short-circuits the subquery.

**#2341 MERGED 2026-07-30 as squash `b348aa89`** (pi-review: bug_free 87, 0 blockers, tests_adequate). Prod-verify OWED. Both blockers below were fixed by moving the claim to the chokepoint and adding a shared cursor.

**The two blockers (both the same mistake: the check went at a read seam, not the chokepoint):**
1. **Lookup/create race.** `findMatchingBehaviorActivations` is an unlocked SELECT; the actual serializer is `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('behavior_event_run'), watcherId)` in `createBehaviorEventRun` (`runs/queue-service.ts:623`), which runs later. Two concurrent deliveries both pass before either run exists. FIXED: the claim moved into `createBehaviorEventRun` under that existing lock, AFTER dedupe and coalesce (neither restarts the Behavior, so neither consumes the window).
2. **`reply_to_source` Behaviors accumulate no cooldown history.** `planBehaviorActivations` splits reply targets off and `message-handler-bridge.ts:717` routes them through the chat transport, never `createBehaviorEventRun` — so no `behavior` run row with `watcher_id` is written and the `NOT EXISTS` never sees them. Cooldown works on background Behaviors and is a silent no-op on reply ones. FIXED by recording history for reply targets rather than rejecting the field: a new nullable cursor `watchers.last_event_activation_at`, claimed by BOTH paths through `behaviors/cooldown.ts`. Rejecting at write time was the alternative and was worse — triggers are editable independently of the cooldown, so a Behavior would accept the field on some triggers and refuse it on others.

**Why a new column and not an existing one:** `last_fired_at` is stamped when a run reaches a TERMINAL state, so a burst would not be debounced by the run it just started; `runs.created_at` cannot see reply Behaviors at all (no run row). `MatchingBehaviorActivation.minCooldownSeconds` rides the match as a feature-enabled hint so the 0 default costs no round-trip; the window is still re-read under the lock.

**Two things review-fix corrected and was right about:** use `clock_timestamp()` not `now()` (a long outer transaction — `insertEvent`'s — would otherwise measure from transaction start), and PROPAGATE a claim DB failure instead of returning false. Returning false silently drops the user's message; propagating lets the delivery retry, matches the AGENTS fail-closed rule, and is consistent with `queueBehaviorActivations` in the same handler, which already throws.

**Mutation-testing trap worth remembering:** the "cooldown is per-Behavior" test first used a sibling with cooldown 0, which short-circuits before reaching the `recent.watcher_id = w.id` predicate — so the unscoped-cooldown mutant SURVIVED. A scoping test must give every participant a non-zero cooldown. The zero short-circuit is a genuine equivalent mutant (a zero-second window can never match a past row); documented at the call site.

**Backtick trap:** a SQL comment inside a postgres.js tagged template cannot contain a backtick — it terminates the template literal. Cost one confusing "Tests no tests" esbuild failure.

See [[project_behavior_run_sdk_approval_gate]], [[feedback_mutation_test_new_tests]].

content.text:
The corrected harness is producing real data now. The smoke run alone already surfaced something worth flagging before the full numbers land.

## The double-post is the model's *default*, not an occasional slip

In arms S and T — where terminal text is delivered **and** `send_message` exists, i.e. exactly production's pre-#2403 configuration — every single "speak" scenario came back `delivered=2`:

```
S ask-mrr     delivered=2 DOUBLE-POST     T ask-mrr     delivered=2 DOUBLE-POST
S ask-direct  delivered=2 DOUBLE-POST     T ask-direct  delivered=2 DOUBLE-POST
S ask-owner   delivered=2 DOUBLE-POST
S ask-status  delivered=2 DOUBLE-POST
```

That's your Slack bug reproduced in a clean room, on 6 of 6 attempts. The model answers via the tool and *then* writes a terminal summary — not because a prompt was missing, but because that's what it does when both channels are live. It's structural, which is why the semantic fix ("tell it not to summarize") was never going to hold and why #2403 had to be a delivery-layer decision.

Arm I can't produce that row by construction — terminal text is never delivered, so `delivered` is capped at whatever it actually sent.

The sentinel arm also looks dead on arrival: 4/4 false-posts on ordinary chatter, meaning it neither stayed quiet **nor** emitted `NO_REPLY`. Same failure I saw in the first smoke, now with a working harness underneath it.

## Memory correction

On re-reading, my cooldown note was correct and I misread it — "event-only" meant *event vs. cron*, and chat messages are event activations. Line 26 of that note already recorded reply targets being wired in. I've rewritten the description so the filename can't mislead the next session the same way, and added the per-Behavior scope limit, which is the part that actually constrains ambient mode.

So the corrected scoreboard on what I told you: the Telegram gap and the harness bugs were real; the cooldown caveat was my error, not the code's.

**Confidence:** high (90) that the double-post is model-default behavior — 6/6 in a clean room plus the production evidence in your DM. Medium (55) on the arm ranking until the 3-trial run finishes; one trial per cell is still one trial.

**Next:**
1. Full 3-trial table when it lands — the false-post/false-silence split across arms is the number that decides the recommendation.
2. Scope call on ambient: Slack-first vs. also solving the streaming layer.
3. Per-conversation cooldown keying, if ambient goes ahead.
4. Delete `examples/lobu-crm/evals/silence-spike-v2.ts` once the run exits — it's in the repo again because scratchpad broke module resolution.

content.text:
Confirmed against `origin/main`. Here's your answer.

## No — joining creates nothing, and nothing is scraped

Three separate things that sound like they'd cover this, and none of them do:

**Membership sync exists, but it's ACL-only.** `slack-acl-sync.ts` polls `conversations.members` per bound channel and materializes `member_of` edges for the authz graph. Those edges are keyed by the raw Slack id (`T…:U…`). No entity, no name, no profile — it exists to decide who's *allowed to see* a channel, not who anyone *is*.

**`member_joined_channel` is subscribed but never handled.** It's in the OAuth scope list at `packages/connectors/src/slack.ts:68`, so Slack sends it. `git grep` on `origin/main` across `packages/server` and `packages/core` returns nothing — there is no handler. The event arrives and is dropped.

**Person entities are minted on *speech*, not membership.** `sender-identity.ts:55` is on the transcript path: it turns an inbound message *author* into a `person` entity, minting on a miss. So someone becomes known the first time they post. A member who has never spoken doesn't exist to the agent.

And even for people who *have* spoken, the minted entity carries **only the Slack user id**. `usersInfo` (`slack-web.ts:197`) requests `users.info` but extracts exactly two fields — `is_admin` and `is_owner`, for the workspace-claim flow. No `real_name`, no `display_name`, no email, no title. Nothing in `slack-web.ts` touches `users.profile` at all.

So in lobusandbox the agent doesn't know the members because there's nothing to know: silent members have no record, and vocal ones have a bare opaque id. That's the gap — it's a missing feature, not a misconfiguration.

## The spike finished, and it refutes what I recommended

I need to correct this before you build on it, because you agreed to a model the data doesn't support.

```
arm  falsePost  falseSilence  doublePost   (lower is better)
S    12/12      0/12          22/24        sentinel  — total failure
T     0/12      0/12          12/24        skip tool — perfect judgment
I     9/12      2/12           1/24        inverted  — my recommendation
```

Arm I — the "terminal text is never delivered, `send_message` is the only way to speak" design I argued for — **false-posted on 9 of 12 chatter messages**. I checked the raw rows to rule out another harness bug; they're real replies:

> `chatter-lunch → "12:30 works for me! Where are we thinking?"`
> `chatter-lunch → "Hey Sarah! I'm just a coding assistant, so I'll have to pass on lunch 😄"`

My reasoning was that making speech an affirmative act would make silence the cheap default. That's wrong. Removing the terminal channel didn't make the model quieter — it just **redirected** the urge to respond into the tool. The bias toward acting isn't a property of *which* channel exists; it's a property of the model.

Arm T won cleanly: 0 false posts, 0 false silence. On the same lunch message it called `skip_reply` all three times. The difference is that "decline" is an **explicit, callable action**. "Just say nothing" isn't salient to a model; `skip_reply` is. An explicit decline affordance beats an implicit one — the opposite of what I predicted.

The one real knock on T is `doublePost 12/24` — it answers via the tool *and* emits terminal text. But that's precisely what #2403 already fixes at the delivery layer. So the design is **T's explicit skip tool + #2403's dedupe**, not the inverted mode.

**Confidence:** high (90) on the Slack findings — `origin/main` grep for the absence, and the two extracted fields read from source. Medium-high (75) on the arm ranking: n=3 per cell on one model, and the arms differ enough that the ordering is unlikely to flip, though exact rates will move.

**Next:**
1. Slack member ingestion is a real feature gap — worth scoping (handle `member_joined_channel`, backfill via `conversations.members`, pull profile fields). Say the word and I'll spec it.
2. Ambient mode should now be specced as `skip_reply` + `is_mention` hard gate, not the inverted design.
3. Re-run the spike on a second model to check the T-over-I ordering isn't glm-specific.
4. `examples/lobu-crm/evals/silence-spike-v2.ts` + results JSON still need deleting from the repo.
