<!-- Per-repo agent rules loaded into every Claude Code session in this repo. Inlines AGENTS.md (shared project rules) first, then layers local-only notes below. User memory entries live under ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/. Don't add anything here unless it's only relevant to Claude agent specific. If other harnesses like pi or codex need it, modify AGENTS.md -->

@AGENTS.md

content.content:
## Repo map
- Bun workspace under `packages/*`; TS source is in `src`, tests in `__tests__`.
- Main packages: `core` shared types/utils, `plugin-api` native plugin contracts, `plugin-host` deterministic plugin composition, `server` gateway + embedded runtime, `agent-worker` Lobu agent execution, `connectors` built-in connectors, `owletto` frontend submodule.
- Before editing a package, read its nearest `AGENTS.md` if present.
- `docs/GOTCHAS.md` collects the mechanical traps (build, SQL, testing, submodule, browser) that have each cost a debugging session. Skim the section for the surface you are touching before you start, and grep it when something looks inexplicable.

## Hard invariants
- **Never write to `~/Code/lobu` directly — work in a worktree.** Run `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` first, and never `git switch` in the main checkout.
- One branch = one concern (not one file). Tangential task → commit/push/open current work, then branch fresh from `main`. Split only for genuinely independent concerns or an unreviewable diff.
- **Multi-replica correctness is mandatory.** Never put shared required state in an in-memory Map/singleton another replica must read or mutate. If a feature relies on cross-pod visibility, use Postgres-mediated state/signal.
- **`events` is append-only.** Never `DELETE FROM events`; tombstone/supersede instead.
- **Request paths never aggregate history.** No `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT ON`, per-row `regexp_*`, or leading-wildcard `LIKE` over an append-only / run-history table (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`, …) on a user-facing read path. History only grows, so read-time aggregation cost grows with it while the answer stays bounded. Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index; run the one-time aggregation in a migration, never per request. Aggregating bounded config tables (`connections`, `watchers`, `agent_users`) is fine.
- **Never bulk-delete prod `organization` rows**, including zero-activity ones — empty-looking orgs are frequently real human signups. Surface them one at a time for confirmation.
- **Workers never receive real credentials.** They may receive only placeholders/proxied access. The only exceptions are device-pinned connectors and short-lived provider-derived credential leases (see `packages/server/AGENTS.md`); a durable stored credential is never one of them.
- Default to static `import`. New dynamic imports require measured cost justification here or in the package AGENTS plus a rationale comment at the call site. Tests may dynamically import after mocks.
  - Node-version gate exceptions: `packages/cli/bin/lobu.js` defers the existing CLI graph without duplicating it, and `packages/server/src/server-entry.ts` adds an 842-byte gate in front of the 4.34 MB server graph (measured 2026-07-24). Both call sites must stay dependency-free until their checks pass.
- Bug fixes require red→fix→green evidence, with both outputs pasted into the PR body. If you cannot reproduce, stop and report the dead end — do not ship a speculative fix.
- Never report done off a green typecheck. Boot it, exercise every branch you touched, clean up test data. If "compiles" is all you ran, say so explicitly.
- Gates are non-negotiable (sequence in "Ship a change" below). `make pre-pr` builds first — that build step is what protects against a stale-dist false green. `make review` is an LLM verdict only: it does NOT run typecheck/knip/tests and is not proof CI will pass.
- The agent-facing product name is **Behavior**; `watcher` is internal engine/DB vocabulary. It must not appear in MCP tool schemas/names/descriptions, ClientSDK discovery metadata, or the connector-sdk public reaction contract — `make pre-pr` fails on it. Internal identifiers (`actingWatcherId`, table/column names, comments) are fine.
- `make review-fix` is the unposted fixer pass and runs BEFORE the first `make review`; verify its diff and commit it. Never iterate `make review` as a find-fix loop — each posted round costs a review + CI cycle.
- Fix the class, not the instance: on the first hit, grep every other instance and fix in one pass — a diff-scoped reviewer only ever finds the next one. Same root cause twice = stop reviewing, grep-enumerate. A class-wide fix is in scope for the branch that found it and does not count as scope creep.
- **Fail closed on durable dispatch/delivery state.** When a durable coordination or delivery operation fails, its caller must not reinterpret the error as proceed/deliver/skip. Propagate a retry, defer, or terminal-failure outcome with a visible log; if the operation may already have succeeded, reconcile idempotently before retrying. Treat lock timeouts, pool errors, and ambiguous or expired rows as failures, not as "nothing changed."
- **Coordination design brake.** A change that needs a second lock, a second retry/deferral budget, or a prose termination argument to explain why it halts is patching a misplaced check — stop and re-derive where the decision belongs before adding mechanism. Find the chokepoint that already serializes the action (e.g. worker dispatch is serialized by `job-router` on the worker-SSE-owner pod) and put the check there; prefer deleting the state transition over coordinating it, and reuse queue-native retry over hand-rolled hold/requeue.
- **Stage by explicit path; never commit the whole tree of a worktree that hosted other work.** A commit is a snapshot — stale file copies silently revert already-merged PRs. After commit/rebase, `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` must equal the task's intended file list; extra files = stop. Verify a "reverts merged work" review finding by diff direction against `origin/main`, never dismiss it as merge-base noise.

## Ship a change
1. `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` → work in `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/`.
2. Reproduce the bug (red) before fixing it. Fix, then prove green.
3. Test: `make test-unit` (no DB) / `make test-integration` (needs `DATABASE_URL` with pgvector). One file: `bun test <path>`, or `cd packages/server && bunx vitest run <path>` for vitest suites.
4. `make pre-pr` — build, typecheck, knip, lint, exposed-surface naming.
5. `make review-fix` on the settled diff and verify what it changed — it edits the working tree, so re-read the files before trusting them.
6. Stage by explicit path (`git add -- <paths>`, never `-A`), commit, then confirm `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly your intended file list. Extra files = stop.
7. `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create` (fill `.github/pull_request_template.md`; conventional-commit title, e.g. `fix(server): …`).
8. `make review` **once** on the settled HEAD. It posts the `pi-review` status, which is a REQUIRED check.
9. Merge squash once CI is green: `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. Never `--admin` past a check that has not reported.
10. Prod-visible surface? Verify it live after rollout. Set a self-rescheduling `ScheduleWakeup` (~1500s) carrying the rollout gate: poll the deployed SHA, then `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$MERGE_SHA" "$DEPLOYED_SHA"` with `MERGE_SHA=$(gh pr view <n> --json mergeCommit --jq .mergeCommit.oid)`. Two ways this gate silently never opens — **gate on the squash commit, not your branch head** (a squash merge writes a new commit with no ancestry link to the branch, so the branch head exits 1 forever: PR #2280 has identical trees and still fails), and **keep that argument order** (merge commit first; reversed, it accepts a stale deploy). Run the live check when it lands, and write the result back to memory.

## Agent workflow
- Do only what was asked. Delete ephemeral files you create. Do not create `*.md` unless asked.
- Prefer `bun`; do not use npm/yarn/pnpm for repo work.
- Fix unused params by deleting them, not `_`-prefixing.
- Never `git stash`; use WIP commits and squash later.
- Never resolve merge conflicts in the GitHub web UI (it has silently dropped 1000+ lines of feature work). Rebase locally against `origin/main`, then diff against the last real feature commit before squashing — except on submodule-pointer branches, where you must `git merge` (see `docs/GOTCHAS.md`, "Submodule & cross-repo").
- Run mandated gates automatically; never ask permission to run one.
- Show the diff, not a summary. Before claiming done — on your own work or a dispatched agent's — surface `git status` plus `git diff --stat <base>...HEAD`. An agent's self-report is a claim; the diff is the evidence.
- UI PRs owe before/after screenshots, and `gh` cannot upload images inline. Capture before shots from the unmodified branch and after shots from the same booted app (auth recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`), base64-embed the PNGs into one self-contained HTML comparison page, publish it as a claude.ai artifact, and link it from the PR.
- Any subagent with write access (Edit/Write/Bash) runs in its own worktree; only grep/read agents share the parent. Two writing agents must NEVER share a worktree — they overwrite each other's uncommitted work.
- Dispatch code-writing agents through `make task-setup NAME=<slug>` and brief them with the absolute `.claude/worktrees/<slug>/` path. Only task-setup does the submodule branch pinning, post-init `bun install`, `.env` copy, and port allocation.
- Do repetitive multi-file edits (renames, signature changes, import rewrites) inline or with one script. Reserve subagents for read-only breadth or genuinely isolated parallel work.
- Before adding an env var, grep for the one the codebase already reads. Do not rename existing vars to a "cleaner" convention unasked.
- Deleting code needs structural evidence (dangling import, completed migration, superseded impl). Low prod usage is not a delete signal; trace the workflow, not just the import graph — docs and help text are load-bearing too.
- **Absence is never proven by a grep on a working tree.** To prove code does *not* exist, run `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` — the fetch is load-bearing, `origin/main` itself goes stale. Applies to every existence check, including the deletion-evidence rule above.
- Slack link pasted (`slack.com/archives/…?thread_ts=`) → run `scripts/slack-thread-viewer.js "<link>"` first.
- To drive the user's real logged-in browser, use the paired Owletto extension — recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`. Do **not** assume CDP/browser-auth is required.
- Unsure in planning → ask before making conflicting or irreversible choices. Mid-execution, block on a question only for irreversible/destructive actions or decisions that are genuinely the user's; for reversible choices with a clear recommended option, take it and flag the choice in your summary.

## Session efficiency
- Never poll in the foreground (`sleep`/`until`/`while` wait loops, repeated `tail`). Run long waits (dev-server boot, CI, deploys) in the background and act on the completion notification.
- Prefer DOM reads (`get_page_text`, `read_page`, `javascript_tool`) over screenshots; screenshot only when visual layout itself is under test. Screenshots are the #1 context-bloat source.
- Read a file before editing it, and re-read it after any external change (a fixer pass, another agent, a rebase). Blind edits fail and cost a retry round-trip.
- Read PR status compactly: `gh pr view <n> --json number,title,isDraft,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision` plus `gh pr checks <n> --required`. Never `--json statusCheckRollup` — measured on PR 2280 it is 7520 bytes against 861, 8.7x larger and less legible.
- Batch narrow fixes into one commit, verified once at the end of the batch — not per fix. It never justifies skipping a reproducer or a correctness-critical test. For a one-line or config-only change, take one CI snapshot and move on.

Step 1 is implemented and proven. Gates are running.

## What landed

One source file, 48 insertions / 11 deletions, plus a new integration test.

**Bug 1 — soft-deleted entities (real reproducer).** `resolveMembers` matched on `entity_identities` alone. An ordinary entity delete soft-deletes the *entity* but leaves its identity rows live — only a merge repoints them — so a member resolved onto a dead entity, got `member_of` written to it, and never got a replacement minted. Net effect: that person silently disappears from the audience of every channel they're in. Fixed with the `JOIN entities … AND e.deleted_at IS NULL` that `lookupMatches` already had.

Red before the fix:
```
× does not resolve a member onto a SOFT-DELETED entity
  → expected [ 1 ] to not include 1
```

**Bug 2 — ambiguous members.** When one member's claims matched *different* entities, the first-array-hit `break` made the outcome depend on the order a connector happened to push identities. On a read-ACL path that's a mis-grant: a recycled login or stale email would hand one person another's channel access. Now collects all matches, breaks the tie on the source's `primary` namespace, and logs the ambiguity — mirroring the warning `entity-link-upsert` already emits.

I scoped this to a **tie-break** rather than making `primary` govern matching, because the contract at `acl-source.ts:31` explicitly says collapsing onto *any* identity is intended. That corrects what I told you earlier — `resolveMembers` wasn't violating its contract, it just had undefined behavior in the ambiguous case.

## Evidence quality

The ambiguity test **passed before the fix too** — `github_user_id` happens to be pushed first, so primary was winning by accident. That makes it a guard test, not a reproducer, so I mutation-tested it (`primaryHit ?? secondaryHit` → reversed) and confirmed it fails. Not vacuous.

Full authz suite: **90+ tests across 14 files, all passing** — including the Slack channel graph, GitHub repo graph, visibility gate, and signin identity-collapse suites that ride the same engine.

Worth noting for the other steps: `make build` silently does nothing (there's no such target — it's `build-packages`), and a fresh worktree ships without workspace dists, so integration tests fail with a misleading module-resolution error until you build. Cost me two false starts.

**Confidence:** high (92) — red→green on the real bug, mutation-tested guard, full suite green on a real Postgres.

**Next:** pre-pr result, then commit and PR. Then step 3 (name enrichment) — which touches the same file, so it goes on top of this rather than in parallel.

`packages/server/src/identity/` has the architecture you're describing: assurance levels (`oauth_verified` vs weaker), a per-connector **capability registry** that caps what each connector is allowed to claim (so a buggy connector can't assert `email` it didn't verify), claim-collision handling, provenance pointing back to the source event, revocation when a fact is superseded, and a shadow mode for validating before enabling writes.

The catch: `identity/connectors/` contains exactly **one file — `google.ts`**. Google emits verified `email` and `hosted_domain`. Slack, Telegram, GitHub, Jira, Linear emit nothing into it.

So the long-term approach isn't "design an identity graph." It's **register connectors into the one that exists**, and close one structural gap.

## The gap that matters most

`$member` — the signed-in human, the natural hub — stores its email in **metadata**, not as an `entity_identities` row. Only the Gmail connector ever writes an `email`-namespace identity.

That means the single universal join key isn't in the join table for the most important entity type. Every connector that knows a person's email currently collapses onto some `person` entity instead of onto the actual human. Fixing that one thing does more for the graph than any new connector work.

## Telegram ↔ Slack: the honest answer

This is where it stops being an architecture question. **Telegram's bot API exposes no email and no phone.** There is no shared identifier between a Telegram user and a Slack user. No graph design creates a join key the provider doesn't emit.

So connectors split into three tiers:

**Tier 1 — auto-collapse on verified email.** Slack (with the scope), Google, GitHub, **Jira, Linear**, and essentially every SaaS work tool. These join deterministically and for free once email is a real identity. Jira and Linear are nearly zero marginal work — same pattern, different fetch.

**Tier 2 — no shared key: requires an act of linking.** Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, SMS. The only sound joins are the human signing in and linking their account, or a human approving a proposal. This is the piece that genuinely doesn't exist yet, and it's the real long-term investment: a "link your Telegram" flow from an authenticated session that writes `telegram_user_id` onto the `$member` at asserted-by-the-user assurance.

**Tier 3 — never automatic.** Display-name, handle, or avatar similarity. Proposal for review only.

## The constraint that should govern all of it

`member_of` edges are a **read ACL**. A wrong join isn't a data-quality blemish — it hands one person another person's channel history. That's exactly why the assurance system exists, and it's the reason I'd resist any heuristic auto-merging on names or handles, however tempting the coverage looks.

It also implies a precedence rule that isn't there today: `email` is unique-per-org, so it's currently **first-writer-wins**. A scraped email could squat the key ahead of a verified one. Assurance should decide who owns a claim, not arrival order — the same class of bug as the ordering issue I just fixed in the ACL matcher.

## The sequence I'd suggest

Write email as an identity on `$member` → register Slack in the capability registry (the scope work already planned) → Jira/Linear/GitHub follow the same pattern nearly free → build the account-linking flow for the tier-2 connectors that can never join on their own.

**Confidence:** high (90) that the engine exists as described and only Google is registered — read the headers, the registry, and listed the directory. Medium (70) on the `$member` email-identity gap; grep-based, same finding the teammate flagged at low confidence, so worth confirming directly before building on it.

**Next:** commit and PR the matcher fix (pre-pr green), then step 3.

content.text:
That corrects me — and confirms your model. `subject-identities.ts:220-222` writes **both** identities onto `$member`:

```ts
await writeIdentities(sql, organizationId, memberEntityId, "auth:signup", [
  { namespace: "auth_user_id", identifier: subject.userId },
  { namespace: "email", identifier: subject.email.toLowerCase() },
]);
```

So `$member` **does** get an email identity. My earlier "email lives only in metadata" came from reading `member-entity.ts` alone and missing this second writer. And the test names confirm the rest of your model is built:

- *collapses the workspace member onto the existing `$member`, never forking a person*
- ***ADOPTS** a `slack_user_id` already owned by a connector-minted person onto the `$member`*
- *leaves a `slack_user_id` owned by a DIFFERENT `$member` untouched (fail closed, never steal)*

So the architecture you remember exists and works: connector mints a `person` carrying its provider id → when that human signs in, the `$member` **adopts** that provider claim → everything consolidates on `$member`, and it refuses to steal a claim owned by someone else. That's the identity graph, already shipped.

**What that means for the Slack work:** the hollow `T…:U…` person isn't an architectural hole — it's the *pre-consolidation* state for someone who hasn't signed in yet. It resolves itself the moment they do. So the real value of email enrichment is narrower than I framed it: it collapses people who will *never* sign in (external collaborators, teammates who only use Slack), and it makes them legible in the meantime.

## On lazy resolution

I'd split it by what the data is *for*, because one half can't be lazy:

**`member_of` edges must stay eager.** They're a read ACL consulted on every recall query. If they only materialize when an agent happens to scrape, the visibility gate fails closed for everyone who hasn't been scraped yet — the bot would tell people it can't see channels they're plainly in. That's the reliability problem you're pointing at, and it's structural rather than a matter of the agent behaving well.

**Profile attributes can be lazy.** Name, title, timezone, avatar are decoration. Fetching them on demand — "who's in this channel?" triggers a `users.list` — is genuinely simpler, avoids bulk-collecting people who never interact, and costs nothing when nobody asks.

**Email sits awkwardly in between.** It's not decoration, because it's the join key — so lazy email means lazy consolidation, which means a person is forked into two entities until someone asks. If a requester resolves to their `$member` while the edge sits on the un-consolidated `person`, the gate denies them. Intermittent false denials are worse than a slightly stale profile.

So: eager edges, eager email, lazy everything else. That keeps the reliable part deterministic and makes the expensive-but-cosmetic part on-demand — which I think is the version of your idea that survives contact with the ACL.

**Confidence:** high (90) — read the identity write and the collapse test names directly. This supersedes my earlier `$member`-has-no-email claim, which was wrong.

**Next:** commit and PR the matcher fix (pre-pr green). Given the above, step 3 is worth re-scoping — name enrichment still earns its place, but the email case is narrower than I sold it.

content.text:
Now I can trace these properly. Adoption moves the identity row from the `person` to the `$member` (keeping a `merged_from_entity_id` trail), and refuses if another `$member` already holds it.

## Case 1 — Slack teammate who never signs in

ACL sync enumerates the channel, mints a `person` carrying `slack_user_id`, writes `member_of` → channel. Today that person is named `T09ABC:U123XYZ`; after the name-enrichment step it's their real name. They're a legible audience member, and recall gating works. No email, so no link to anything else. **Works today.**

## Case 2 — That person signs in *via Slack*

`$member` is created/found by email, gets `auth_user_id` + `email` identities, and **adopts** `slack_user_id` off the `person`. Consolidated exactly as you remembered.

One wrinkle worth knowing: adoption moves the *identity* but leaves the old `person` entity behind, and its `member_of` edges are **not** repointed. The next ACL sync resolves `slack_user_id` → now the `$member`, writes the edge there, and reconciles the stale one away. So it self-heals — but there's a **window of up to 15 minutes after signing in where the person may be denied access to channels they're plainly in**, because their `$member` has no edge yet and the gate fails closed. That's a real UX bug, and it's independent of everything else we've discussed.

## Case 3 — They sign in via **Google** instead

`$member` gets `auth_user_id` + `email`. But adoption is Slack-sign-in-specific — nothing moves `slack_user_id`. The Slack `person` keeps it, ACL sync keeps resolving to that `person`, and the human stays **permanently forked**: a `$member` on one side, a Slack `person` on the other, no join.

**This is the concrete case that justifies email enrichment.** If the Slack member carried an `email` identity, `resolveMembers` would match the `$member`'s email and collapse them. Without it, anyone who signs in via anything other than Slack never consolidates. That's a much sharper argument than the "hollow names" framing I was using.

## Case 4 — Telegram user DMs the bot

`buildSenderIdentity` has `case 'slack'` and `default: return null`. **Telegram authors are never attributed to an entity at all** — the message is captured with no `author_entity_id`. So today there's nothing to link. Before Telegram↔Slack linking is even a question, Telegram needs to mint identities in the first place.

## Case 5 — "Who is in #sales?"

Agent reads entities with `member_of` → the channel's `$resource`. Returns whoever the graph holds — real names after step 3, `$member`s for people who signed in via Slack, `person`s otherwise. This is the query that currently looks broken to you, and step 3 alone fixes the visible symptom.

## Case 6 — Someone leaves the channel

Next sync's departure reconcile soft-deletes their `member_of` edge; recall access drops. **Works today**, and it's why the sync has to stay eager.

## Case 7 — Conflict: two humans, one Slack id

Adoption refuses to take a claim held by another `$member` — fail closed, never steal. Correct as-is.

## What the cases actually tell us

The ordering I gave you earlier holds, but the *reasons* shift. Name enrichment (step 3) fixes Case 5, the visible one. Email enrichment (step 4) exists to fix **Case 3**, not the hollow names — non-Slack sign-in is the permanent fork. Case 4 is a prerequisite nobody has scoped: Telegram doesn't mint identities, so it can't participate in the graph yet. And Case 2 surfaces a fresh bug — the post-sign-in access gap — that isn't on any list.

**Confidence:** high (90) on cases 1, 2, 4, 7 — read the adoption SQL, the sender-identity switch, and the reconcile path. Medium (70) on the Case 2 timing window: the mechanism is clear but I haven't measured whether some other path repoints edges sooner.

**Next:** worth deciding whether the Case 2 gap and Case 4 (Telegram identities) join the queue — the first is a live bug, the second is the actual blocker for the cross-connector linking you're after.

## 1. The post-signin access window — **the user IS denied, for up to 15 minutes. No fallback covers them.** (verified)

**(a) There is no signin-triggered ACL resync.** `runAclSyncTick` has exactly one production caller:

- `packages/server/src/scheduled/jobs.ts:193-199` → `scheduler.register('authz-acl-sync', …, { cron: '*/15 * * * *' })`
- `packages/server/src/authz/acl-sync.ts:21-33` fans out to `runSlackAclSyncTick` / `runGithubAclSyncTick`
- `buildAccessGraph` has exactly two callers: `packages/server/src/authz/slack-acl-sync.ts:238` and `packages/server/src/authz/github-acl-sync.ts:91` — both reachable only from that cron tick.

The signin hook (`packages/server/src/auth/index.tsx:896` in `account.create.after`, and `:935` in `account.update.after`) fires `void persistLoginSlackIdentity(accountSummary)` and nothing else. No graph rebuild, no edge write, no cache bust. Slack's `member_joined_channel` appears only as a subscribed-event string in the connector manifest (`packages/connectors/src/slack.ts:68`) — it is not wired to a graph rebuild.

**(b) No resolver path finds the old person's edges.** Two independent gates, both fail:

- `resolveRequesterMember` (`packages/server/src/authz/channel-visibility.ts:154-164`) tries the auth claim **first** (line 161). Post-signin that succeeds and returns the `$member` — so line 163's `resolveRequesterByChatUserId` fallback is **never reached**. And even if it were, the `slack_user_id` claim it looks up (line 123-135) now points at the `$member` too, because adoption moved it. Neither path can reach the orphan `person`.
- `getVisibleChannelKeysForMember` (`channel-visibility.ts:178-201`) then queries `entity_relationships … WHERE r.from_entity_id = ${memberEntityId}` — the `$member`, which has **zero** `member_of` edges. Empty set.
- `filterChannelsForRequester:251-263`: `visibleKeys` is empty → every row on an `enforced` connection is dropped at line 262.
- The SQL twin, `packages/server/src/authz/channel-messages-visibility.ts:67-84` + `:121` (`rr.from_entity_id = ${requesterMemberSubquery}`), hard-filters on `et.slug = '$member'` and `source_connector = 'auth:signup'`. Same outcome, no chat-user fallback at all (documented at lines 25-27).

**(c) Verdict.** A user who signs in with Slack is denied every enforced channel until the next `*/15` tick — worst case ~15 min, mean ~7.5 min, longer if the tick fails (`syncSlackConnectionAcl` marks `failed` on any systemic error, `slack-acl-sync.ts:250-261`).

**Severity nuance (important):** this is a *missed improvement*, not a regression. Before adoption the `$member` also had no `member_of` edges (the edges were on the `person`), so the user saw nothing then either. Adoption's whole purpose is to make the *next* tick attach the edges to the `$member`. The gap is that the fix is asynchronous with no synchronous kick — and the comment at `subject-identities.ts:85-88` ("the edges follow the claim… on the next sync tick") acknowledges this deliberately, but the window is undocumented in user-facing terms.

**One real hole in that reasoning:** `syncSlackConnectionAcl` only graphs channels returned by `resolveBoundChannelRows` (`slack-acl-sync.ts:117-120`). If the connection has zero bound Slack rows, it returns `{ok: true, teamsSynced: 0}` at line 158 **without calling `buildAccessGraph`** — so `markAclEnforced` never re-stamps and, more importantly, the `$member` never gets edges. Meanwhile `getConnectionEnforcement` still sees the previously-stamped row. Whether that combination goes stale-and-fail-closed or stays enforced-and-empty depends on the freshness window in `acl-state.ts`, which I did not read. **Flagged as unverified.**

---

## 2. Orphaned `person` entities — **nothing cleans them up; stale edges mostly self-heal; one narrow escalation path** (verified except where noted)

**Nothing merges, tombstones, or repoints the orphan.** `adoptSlackIdentityOntoMember` (`subject-identities.ts:120-141`) issues a single `UPDATE entity_identities`. It does **not** set `entities.merged_into`, does not soft-delete the person, does not touch `entity_relationships`. There is no orphan-person reaper anywhere in `packages/server/src/scheduled/` (I enumerated the directory) and `git grep orphan origin/main` returns only unrelated worker/secret/queue orphan handling. `applyMergeGroup` / `applyMerge` (`packages/server/src/utils/entity-merge.ts`) are invoked only from the two admin tools `entity-field-approval.ts:47` and `manage_entity.ts:59` — never from the signin path.

So the orphan retains: its `member_of` edges, its `entities.metadata` (which still contains a **stale copy** of `slack_user_id` — written at creation by `access-graph.ts:192`, `metadata[id.namespace] = id.value`, and never cleaned), its name, and any identities from other namespaces.

**Do the stale edges get reconciled away?** Mostly yes. `buildAccessGraph`'s departure reconcile (`access-graph.ts:390-404`) soft-deletes `member_of` edges `WHERE to_entity_id = ${resourceEntityId} AND from_entity_id <> ALL(keep)`. On the next tick `resolveMembers` (`access-graph.ts:134-184`) resolves `T…:U…` → the `$member` (identity-first, type-agnostic), so the orphan is absent from `keep` and its edge to that resource is deleted, while the `$member` gains one. **Self-healing, but scoped to resources present in the current build** — `currentMembersByResource` is only populated for the resources passed in (`:355-359`). An edge to a channel that has since been unbound, or whose resource entity failed to resolve (`:357` `continue`), survives indefinitely.

**Could a stale edge grant access to someone?** Enumerating every resolver that could land on the orphan:

- `resolveRequesterMemberEntityId` (`channel-visibility.ts:59-84`) — joins `et.slug = '$member'`. Orphan is `person`. **No.**
- `channel-messages-visibility.ts:74-77` — same `$member` filter. **No.**
- `resolvableMemberClaimExists` (`packages/server/src/authz/member-claim-predicate.ts:29-48`) — same. **No.**
- `resolveRequesterByChatUserId` (`channel-visibility.ts:100-139`) — **this is the one resolver with NO entity-type filter.** It resolves purely on `(namespace, identifier)`. Post-adoption the adopted key points at the `$member`, so the orphan is unreachable *via that team's key*. It becomes reachable only if the orphan holds a `slack_user_id` for a *different* enforcing team — possible in principle because `resolveSenderIdentity` (`entity-link-upsert.ts:963-1000`) and `applyEventAttributions` can attach additional identities to an existing `person` over time. Probability is low; the consequence is a genuine cross-workspace read leak. Worth a follow-up.

**Second-order risk (inferred):** the orphan's stale `metadata.slack_user_id` makes it look like the real Slack user in entity lists and agent-facing entity reads, and the person keeps its display name. From the UI this reads as a duplicate human that never goes away.

## 3. Attribution split-brain — **real, and nothing repoints it** (verified)

`channel_messages.author_entity_id` is stamped at capture time by `resolveSenderIdentity` (`entity-link-upsert.ts:963`), which is explicitly type-agnostic (comment at `:951-960`): it returns whatever entity owns the `slack_user_id`. So:

- messages captured **before** signin → `author_entity_id = person`
- messages captured **after** signin → `author_entity_id = $member`

**Nothing repoints history.** `entity-merge.ts` contains **zero** references to `channel_messages` (grepped: `channel_messages|FROM events|UPDATE events|session_calls` returns nothing in that file) — so even a genuine admin merge would not fix it, and adoption isn't a merge anyway.

What actually breaks, per read path:

- **`channel_messages` reads — degraded but not broken.** `author_entity_id` is only ever *projected*, never filtered on. `packages/server/src/tools/search.ts:557,579` selects it; `packages/server/src/watchers/source-refs.ts:385` selects it; `packages/server/src/utils/table-schema.ts:653` exposes it to `query_sql`. My grep for `author_entity_id` in a WHERE/JOIN position across the repo returned **nothing**. So the failure mode is an agent receiving two different entity ids for the same human across one transcript — bad for "who said this" / entity-timeline joins the agent builds itself, not a filter miss.
- **`events` recall — half self-heals.** `entityLinkMatchSql` (`packages/server/src/utils/content-search/entity-link.ts:53-83`) has two branch families:
  - The **identity branch** (`:70-76`) joins `entity_identities ei ON ei.entity_id = ${paramRef} AND ei.namespace = '<ns>'` against `events.metadata->>ns`. Because the identity *row moved*, querying the `$member` now matches **all** historical events carrying that `slack_user_id`, and querying the orphan matches none. `slack_user_id` is in `STANDARD_IDENTITY_NAMESPACES` (`:28-31`, fed by `slackIdentityModule.recallNamespaces`, `slack-identity.ts:83`). **This branch fixes itself for free.**
  - The **direct branch** (`:66-70`) matches `events.entity_ids && ARRAY(SELECT id FROM entities WHERE id = X OR merged_into = X)`. Adoption never sets `merged_into` on the orphan, so events raw-stamped with `entity_ids = [person]` (save_content memories, feed-pinned, webhook attributions — the comment at `:14-18` names them) **do not recall against the `$member`, permanently.** They stay stranded on the orphan.
  - Same asymmetry applies to `get_behavior.ts:532,839`, which reuses the same namespace list.

Net: identity-graph-attributed recall converges; raw `entity_ids`-stamped recall is permanently split. Setting `entities.merged_into = $member` on the orphan would close the direct branch for free via the existing redirect — and adoption already writes `merged_from_entity_id` on the identity row (`subject-identities.ts:127`), so half the provenance trail exists but the half the read path actually consults does not.

**Verified in repo:** nothing — Telegram is a 35-line declaration with no API surface beyond `botToken`/`mode`.

**Provider knowledge (not verified against live API — flag as such):**
- The Bot API `User` object carries `id` (int64, **globally unique**, unlike Slack), `is_bot`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `username`, `language_code`, `is_premium`. **No email. No phone.**

- **Email requires Telegram Passport** (encrypted `PassportElementTypeEmail`, separate public-key setup + explicit user consent). Not practical.
- The **Login Widget / Login URL** returns id/first_name/last_name/username/photo_url — still no email.
- **Group membership cannot be enumerated.** The Bot API has `getChatMember(chat_id, user_id)`, `getChatAdministrators`, and `getChatMemberCount` — there is **no list-all-members endpoint**. A Telegram `AclSourceDef` in the Slack shape (`AccessResource.members` = complete audience, `acl-source.ts:57-63`) is therefore **not constructible**. You could only accrete membership observationally from `new_chat_members` / `left_chat_member` / message senders, which fails open for lurkers and is not an authoritative snapshot. **Do not model Telegram as an ACL source.**
- Edge cases to handle: anonymous group admins and channel posts arrive with `sender_chat` and no `from`; `username` is mutable and reusable (must be secondary/`matchOnly`, never `primary`).

const model = channelReadIdentityFor(sender.platform);
if (!model) return null;
const key = model.buildUserKey(sender.teamId, sender.authorId);
if (!key) return null;

# Identity linking, sign-in providers, and the identity engine — findings

All absence claims below verified with `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` (repo at `1f5213b3d`). Owletto is a submodule, so `git grep origin/main -- packages/owletto/**` returns nothing by design; I grepped inside the submodule checkout separately (`packages/owletto` @ `49a9909d`).

## 1. Is there a user-facing account-linking surface? — YES, one, and it is not the one you'd expect

The premise "no linking surface" is **wrong**, but the surface that exists writes to a *completely different table* than `entity_identities` and never touches the `$member` entity graph.

**The `/lobu link <code>` flow** — a signed-in human proving "this chat account is me":

- Mint: `POST /api/:orgSlug/preview/claims` (`packages/server/src/index.ts:1076` → `createPreviewClaim`, `packages/server/src/preview/slack.ts:131`), called by the CLI's `lobu run` (`packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts:803`) under `mcpAuth`. The code lives in `oauth_states`, scope `slack-preview-claim`, 15-min default TTL (`preview/slack.ts:32-36`).
- Redeem: the user pastes the code from their chat account. Two entry points — slash command dispatch, and plain message text for DMs where Slack won't deliver a slash command (`packages/server/src/gateway/connections/message-handler-bridge.ts:1013-1031`, gated on `connection.settings.previewMode === true`).
- Write: `packages/server/src/preview/slack.ts:386-395` calls `linkChatUserIdentity({ platform, teamId, platformUserId, lobuUserId: claim.createdBy })`.

**Target table is `chat_user_identities`**, not `entity_identities`: `packages/server/src/lobu/stores/chat-identity.ts:60-77`. PK `(platform, team_id, platform_user_id)`, FK to `"user"(id)` (`db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:655, 2748, 4691`). The module docblock explicitly states it is platform-agnostic ("Slack, Telegram, or a custom connector all link the same way") and explicitly **not** cross-platform consolidation.

Despite platform-agnostic plumbing, the only platforms reachable today are Slack and Telegram — `PREVIEW_PLATFORMS = MANAGED_CHAT_PLATFORMS_SET` with join defaults for exactly those two (`preview/slack.ts:38-46`). No Discord/GitHub path.

The provenance is honest about being weak. `preview/slack.ts:374-385`:
> "The code was minted by an authenticated `lobu run` and is ASSUMED to be redeemed by the same person… a claim code is effectively a credential for the minter's account — never paste one in a shared channel… **Real identity proof (Slack OAuth / email match) is a follow-up.**"

The takeover guard is the `ON CONFLICT … WHERE chat_user_identities.lobu_user_id = EXCLUDED.lobu_user_id` predicate (`chat-identity.ts:70-76`) — an already-linked triple is never silently re-bound.

Second writer of the same table: `packages/server/src/gateway/connections/slack-claim.ts:197, 230` (Slack workspace-install claim), hardcoded `platform: "slack"`.

**What does NOT exist** (each verified against `origin/main`):

- No settings UI. `packages/owletto/src/app/account/settings.tsx` is Profile (read-only name/email/user id) + Sign Out — nothing else. No `identit*` hits anywhere in owletto that relate to account linking.
- No REST route. `git grep -rln "identit" origin/main -- 'packages/server/src/gateway/routes/**'` → 7 files, all agent-config / agent / agents / app-install / app-webhooks / github-team-graph / github-webhook-actor; none is a linking endpoint.
- No MCP tool. `manage_entity` has merge/unmerge (which *move* identities) but no add-identity operation (`packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-entity.ts`). Tool list at `packages/server/src/tools/admin/index.ts:125-263`.
- `git grep -rniE "link_identity|linkIdentity|claimIdentity|claim_identity|verifyIdentity|verify_identity|addIdentity|add_identity|manage_identities|identity_link|account_link" origin/main` → one hit, an unrelated better-auth error code string at `packages/server/src/auth/index.tsx:851`.

**Every `INSERT INTO entity_identities` in `origin/main`** (non-test) — all seven are machine provenance, none user-asserted:

| Site | Provenance |
|---|---|
| `auth/subject-identities.ts:60` | `auth:signup` — `auth_user_id` + `email` |
| `auth/subject-identities.ts:107` | `auth:signup` — Slack adoption |
| `tools/save_content.ts:326` | `save_content` — self-heals `auth_user_id` from an email match |
| `utils/canvas-events.ts:161` | lazy canvas entity |
| `utils/entity-link-upsert.ts:512` | `connector:<key>` — connector sync |
| `utils/member-entity.ts:136` | member provisioning |
| `utils/promote-keyed-entities.ts:424` | keyed promotion |

One adjacent thing worth knowing: better-auth's own `accountLinking` is enabled (`auth/index.tsx:293-303`, `trustedProviders` = configured socials + generic-OAuth ids, `updateUserInfoOnLink: true`). The login page surfaces this as the `account_not_linked` path — "This social account matches an existing Lobu user. Sign in with a magic link to verify ownership, then continue" (`packages/owletto/src/app/auth/login.tsx:76, 111, 167-172`). That links an OAuth provider to a *better-auth user*, and because it fires `account.create.after`, it does indirectly trigger the Slack adoption + identity ingest. So for the five login-capable providers there is a real user-driven path — just not a general "add an arbitrary account" one.

## 2. Sign-in providers, and what each writes onto `$member`

Provider set is data-driven, not hardcoded: any bundled connector declaring `loginScopes` on an OAuth auth-schema method is a login candidate (`packages/server/src/auth/config.ts:412`, `collectEnabledLoginProviderConfigs` at `:105-175`). `getLoginProviderScopes` (`config.ts`) is now a pass-through — no provider allowlist, it only requires non-empty scopes.

Declared `loginScopes` in `origin/main`:

| Connector | `provider` | Identity written onto `$member` at sign-in |
|---|---|---|
| `google_calendar.ts:110`, `google_gmail.ts:115`, `youtube.ts:270` | `google` (first-wins dedupe per provider) | Identity-engine facts only — `identity_fact` **events**, not `entity_identities` |
| `slack.ts:147` | `slack` (generic-OAuth route, self-describing OIDC) | `slack_user_id` = `T…:U…` in `entity_identities`, source `auth:signup` |
| `github.ts:430` | `github` | **Nothing beyond `auth_user_id` + `email`** |
| `microsoft_outlook.ts:109` | `microsoft` | **Nothing beyond `auth_user_id` + `email`** |
| `x.ts:1854` | `twitter` (keys `TWITTER_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`) | **Nothing beyond `auth_user_id` + `email`** |

Baseline comes from the connector catalog; an org can shadow a provider with its own OAuth app, union-only, never narrowing (`config.ts:459-501`). A global-only allowlist exists via `LOBU_GLOBAL_LOGIN_PROVIDERS` (`config.ts:522-529`), applied only when `organizationId` is null.

**`adoptSlackIdentityOntoMember` is the ONLY provider-specific adoption, and there is no generic version.** `persistLoginSlackIdentity` hard-gates at `packages/server/src/auth/subject-identities.ts:315`:

```ts
if (account.providerId.trim().toLowerCase() !== "slack") return;
```

Its sibling `adoptSlackIdentityOntoMember` (`:100-125`) is a three-step INSERT → adopt-from-`person` → conflict ladder, hardcoded to `SLACK_IDENTITY.USER_ID`. The generic seam that exists is the *identity engine's* capability registry, and only Google is registered there. So github / microsoft / twitter fall through both mechanisms — the codebase already knows this and warns at boot: `auth/index.tsx:169-176` logs `Social provider "X" is enabled but has no identity connector — facts will not be ingested`.

I cannot confirm from the repo which providers actually have credentials in prod. `.env.example` contains no `*_CLIENT_ID` keys, and `charts/lobu/templates/deployment.yaml:104` pulls everything from an out-of-repo `secretRef`. **Flagging as unverified.**

## 3. Identity engine reach — live, not shadow, but nearly inert downstream

**It is wired into a live code path.** `scheduleIdentityIngest` fires from better-auth's `account.create.after` (`auth/index.tsx:893`) and `account.update.after` (`:933`); `scheduleIdentityTombstoneOnAccountDelete` from `account.delete.after` (`:943`). All fire-and-forget — sign-in never blocks (`identity/auth-hook.ts:180-242`). Routing is registry-based; `auth-hook.ts:19` side-effect-imports `./connectors/google`, the only registered connector.

**It is NOT in shadow mode.** `IDENTITY_ENGINE_SHADOW` appears in exactly two places in all of `origin/main` — `identity/engine.ts:16, 113` and `identity/types.ts:31`. It is absent from `.env.example`, `charts/`, and `.github/`. The predicate is `process.env.IDENTITY_ENGINE_SHADOW === "true"` (`engine.ts:111-114`), so unset ⇒ **shadow off ⇒ full mode, derivations and revocations run.** Caveat: the helm chart mounts an out-of-repo Secret via `envFrom`, so an operator *could* have set it in the cluster. **Unverified from the repo** — worth a `kubectl get secret` check.

What shadow would actually suppress is narrow: facts, supersedes, and tombstones are written either way; only step 4 (revoke derivations) and step 5 (apply `auto_create_when` rules) are skipped (`engine.ts:742-751`). So "turning it on" is not a meaningful lever — the engine is already at full power.

**But its blast radius is nearly nil.** `identity_fact` events have exactly two readers in `origin/main`: the engine's own prior-fact query (`engine.ts:278`) and the tombstone-on-delete lookup (`auth-hook.ts:265`). No authz gate, no routing, no read path consumes them. The only externally visible effect is derived relationships from `auto_create_when` rules — and those require an org to have authored rules via `manage_entity_schema` (`packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-entity-schema.ts:6-24`), plus a `targetField` declared `x-identity-namespace` (`findEntitiesByMetadataField` bails with a warn otherwise). **Whether any prod org has such rules is DB state I could not check.**

So concretely, "turning it on" would mean: registering emitters for github/microsoft/slack/twitter in `identity/connectors/`, and authoring `auto_create_when` rules. Neither is an env flag.

## 4. Claim collision — the premise doesn't match the code

`CLAIM_COLLISION_SEMANTIC_TYPE` (`packages/connector-sdk/src/identity-types.ts:281`) does **not** mean "two entities claim the same identity."

Read `engine.ts:830-847` with `findEntitiesByMetadataField` (`engine.ts`, scoped `WHERE e.organization_id = catalogOrgId AND e.metadata->>${field} = ${normalizedValue}`, no entity-type filter) and `validateTypeRule(relationshipTypeId, memberEntityId, match.entityId)`: `memberEntityId` is the FROM side, `match.entityId` the TO side. A collision fires when **one member's verified fact matches ≥2 candidate TARGET entities** under `matchStrategy: "unique_only"` — e.g. an `email_domain` of `acme.com` matching two `company` rows. It is ambiguous relationship-target resolution, not identity contention.

**This is a bug worth flagging.** The event body at `engine.ts:513` says:

```
content: `Two or more candidate $member rows match this provider-verified ${fact.namespace}; manual resolution required.`
```

and the title is `Identity match collision on ${fact.namespace}`. The candidates are not `$member` rows. Any human who reads this card will diagnose the wrong problem.

- The **Login Widget / Login URL** returns id/first_name/last_name/username/photo_url — still no email.

**Both are present.** `packages/connectors/src/jira.ts` (790 lines) and `linear.ts` (511 lines) — full OAuth data connectors with virtual (live JQL/GraphQL pushdown) and collected (`sync()`) feeds.

**Neither participates in identity in any way.** No `attributions`, no `*-identity.ts` module, not in `ACL_SOURCES` (`authz/sources.ts:15`), not in `CONNECTOR_IDENTITY_MODULES` (`connector-identity-modules.ts:27`), not in the capability registry.

### As identity producers — unusually cheap, because they already fetch the joinable key
Both already retrieve email and then **discard it into a display string**:
- Jira: `JiraUser.emailAddress` (`jira.ts:74`) → `actorName` returns `displayName ?? emailAddress` (`jira.ts:157`) → stamped as `author_name` (`jira.ts:661`) and `assignee`/`reporter` (`jira.ts:638-639`).

Because the target namespace is the **generic** `email` (`identity-namespaces.ts:52-58`, already `eventRecallIndexed: true` with an existing index), this needs **no new namespace, no new connector-identity module, and no migration**. The change is:
1. Stamp `metadata.reporter_email` / `metadata.assignee_email` alongside the existing display fields (`jira.ts:635-670`, `linear.ts:450-480`).
2. Add an `EventAttributionRule` on the feed's `eventKinds`, copying the Gmail shape verbatim (`google_gmail.ts:183-212`) — `role: 'authored_by'`, `identities: [{ namespace: 'email', eventPath: 'metadata.reporter_email' }]`.
3. Decide `autoCreate`. Gmail gates on `createWhen: metadata.replied === true` to avoid minting a person per no-reply sender (`google_gmail.ts:196`). For Jira/Linear every actor is a real workspace colleague, so `autoCreate: true` unconditionally is defensible — but that's a product call, not a mechanical one.

**Provider-knowledge caveat (unverified against live APIs):** Jira Cloud **redacts `emailAddress` by default** under its GDPR privacy model — it returns `null` unless the app holds `read:jira-user` *and* the user's profile visibility permits it. The field being typed at `jira.ts:74` is not evidence it's populated in production. Linear's `User.email` is generally returned for workspace members under the standard `read` scope. **Before building this, dump one live payload from each and check whether email is actually non-null.** If Jira's is systematically null, the fallback identity is `accountId` (`jira.ts:75`, currently unused) as a new `jira_account_id` namespace — which then *does* require a connector-identity module and, if recall-indexed, a migration.

### As ACL sources
- **Linear maps cleanly.** `teams { id key members { id email } }` gives resource × complete audience, exactly the `AccessResource` shape (`acl-source.ts:57-63`). A `linearAclSource: AclSourceDef` with `resourceNamespace: 'linear_team_key'` and `memberIdentities: [{namespace:'email', primary:true}]` plus a `linearTeamsToResources()` would be a near-mechanical copy of `githubReposToResources` (`github-identity.ts:140-158`), and an `authz/linear-acl-sync.ts` copying `github-acl-sync.ts:94-97`.
- **Jira does not map cleanly.** Its permission scheme (project roles → actors, which may be groups, plus issue-level security levels) is a materially richer model than "collaborators", and flattening it to a member list will silently over-grant. I'd treat Jira ACL as a separate design task, not a copy of the GitHub source.

Neither should be an ACL source *until* it's an identity producer — an ACL source whose members carry no identity the rest of the graph recognizes gates nothing.

## 3. The generic gap — is the switch the right seam?

**No, and the repo already contains the general mechanism — `buildSenderIdentity`'s Slack case is a verbatim duplicate of it.**

Compare:

```
sender-identity.ts:44-56          slack-identity.ts:110-120
  normalizeSlackUserId(teamId,      buildUserKey: (teamId, userId) =>
    authorId)                         normalizeSlackUserId(teamId, userId)
  namespace: SLACK_IDENTITY          userNamespace: SLACK_IDENTITY.USER_ID
    .USER_ID
```

`ChannelReadIdentity` (`connector-sdk/src/acl-source.ts:87-118`) already carries **exactly** the three things `buildSenderIdentity` needs — `platform`, `userNamespace`, `buildUserKey(teamId, userId)` — it is connector-owned (`slack-identity.ts:110-126`), collected in a platform-keyed registry (`authz/sources.ts:31-42`), and has a working lookup helper `channelReadIdentityFor(platform)`. The entire switch reduces to:

```ts
const model = channelReadIdentityFor(sender.platform);
if (!model) return null;
const key = model.buildUserKey(sender.teamId, sender.authorId);
if (!key) return null;
return { identities: [{ namespace: model.userNamespace, identifier: key,
                        matchOnly: false, primary: false }],
         mintEntityType: 'person' };
```

`mintEntityType: 'person'` is a constant across all platforms today, so nothing is lost.

**The one real objection:** `CHANNEL_READ_IDENTITIES` is documented as *"Chat platforms whose per-channel read gate is **enforced**"* (`authz/sources.ts:28-31`), and it is consumed by `channel-visibility.ts:169` and `channel-messages-visibility.ts:60` to build the visibility gate. Adding Telegram there to get sender attribution would **also switch on a channel read gate for Telegram** — and since Telegram membership can't be enumerated from the Bot API (Q1), that gate would have an empty `member_of` graph and deny everything. Attribution and read-gating are genuinely different capabilities and must not be coupled through one list.

**Recommended shape:** keep `ChannelReadIdentity` as-is for the read gate, and add a separate, smaller optional hook for attribution. The natural home is `ChatPlatformDescriptor` (`gateway/connections/platforms/types.ts:53-57`), whose contract already states *"Adding a platform means adding one module under `./platforms/` and registering it in `./index.ts` — no manager edits"* — every other per-platform capability (`extractRoutingInfo`, `createFileHandler`, `getInstructionProvider`, `configureWebhook`) is already an optional hook there, and `sender-identity.ts`'s switch is the last platform-dispatching `switch` left on this path. Add `buildSenderIdentity?(sender): SenderIdentitySpec | null`, have `platforms/slack.ts` delegate to `slackChannelReadIdentity`, and `sender-identity.ts` becomes `getPlatformDescriptor(platform)?.buildSenderIdentity?.(sender) ?? null`.

**What a second platform must duplicate today** (the cost of leaving the switch): a `*-identity.ts` module (namespaces + normalizer + `ConnectorIdentityModule`), an entry in `CONNECTOR_IDENTITY_MODULES`, a `case` in the switch, a rewrite of the pinned negative test, and — if it declares any recall namespace — a migration or CI/startup fails. Steps 1, 2, and 5 are irreducible (they're the connector genuinely declaring new vocabulary). Steps 3 and 4 are pure duplication that the hook removes.

# Identity linking, sign-in providers, and the identity engine — findings

All absence claims below verified with `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` (repo at `1f5213b3d`). Owletto is a submodule, so `git grep origin/main -- packages/owletto/**` returns nothing by design; I grepped inside the submodule checkout separately (`packages/owletto` @ `49a9909d`).

## 1. Is there a user-facing account-linking surface? — YES, one, and it is not the one you'd expect

The premise "no linking surface" is **wrong**, but the surface that exists writes to a *completely different table* than `entity_identities` and never touches the `$member` entity graph.

**The `/lobu link <code>` flow** — a signed-in human proving "this chat account is me":

- Mint: `POST /api/:orgSlug/preview/claims` (`packages/server/src/index.ts:1076` → `createPreviewClaim`, `packages/server/src/preview/slack.ts:131`), called by the CLI's `lobu run` (`packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts:803`) under `mcpAuth`. The code lives in `oauth_states`, scope `slack-preview-claim`, 15-min default TTL (`preview/slack.ts:32-36`).
- Redeem: the user pastes the code from their chat account. Two entry points — slash command dispatch, and plain message text for DMs where Slack won't deliver a slash command (`packages/server/src/gateway/connections/message-handler-bridge.ts:1013-1031`, gated on `connection.settings.previewMode === true`).
- Write: `packages/server/src/preview/slack.ts:386-395` calls `linkChatUserIdentity({ platform, teamId, platformUserId, lobuUserId: claim.createdBy })`.

**Target table is `chat_user_identities`**, not `entity_identities`: `packages/server/src/lobu/stores/chat-identity.ts:60-77`. PK `(platform, team_id, platform_user_id)`, FK to `"user"(id)` (`db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:655, 2748, 4691`). The module docblock explicitly states it is platform-agnostic ("Slack, Telegram, or a custom connector all link the same way") and explicitly **not** cross-platform consolidation.

Despite platform-agnostic plumbing, the only platforms reachable today are Slack and Telegram — `PREVIEW_PLATFORMS = MANAGED_CHAT_PLATFORMS_SET` with join defaults for exactly those two (`preview/slack.ts:38-46`). No Discord/GitHub path.

The provenance is honest about being weak. `preview/slack.ts:374-385`:
> "The code was minted by an authenticated `lobu run` and is ASSUMED to be redeemed by the same person… a claim code is effectively a credential for the minter's account — never paste one in a shared channel… **Real identity proof (Slack OAuth / email match) is a follow-up.**"

The takeover guard is the `ON CONFLICT … WHERE chat_user_identities.lobu_user_id = EXCLUDED.lobu_user_id` predicate (`chat-identity.ts:70-76`) — an already-linked triple is never silently re-bound.

Second writer of the same table: `packages/server/src/gateway/connections/slack-claim.ts:197, 230` (Slack workspace-install claim), hardcoded `platform: "slack"`.

**What does NOT exist** (each verified against `origin/main`):

- No settings UI. `packages/owletto/src/app/account/settings.tsx` is Profile (read-only name/email/user id) + Sign Out — nothing else. No `identit*` hits anywhere in owletto that relate to account linking.
- No REST route. `git grep -rln "identit" origin/main -- 'packages/server/src/gateway/routes/**'` → 7 files, all agent-config / agent / agents / app-install / app-webhooks / github-team-graph / github-webhook-actor; none is a linking endpoint.
- No MCP tool. `manage_entity` has merge/unmerge (which *move* identities) but no add-identity operation (`packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-entity.ts`). Tool list at `packages/server/src/tools/admin/index.ts:125-263`.
- `git grep -rniE "link_identity|linkIdentity|claimIdentity|claim_identity|verifyIdentity|verify_identity|addIdentity|add_identity|manage_identities|identity_link|account_link" origin/main` → one hit, an unrelated better-auth error code string at `packages/server/src/auth/index.tsx:851`.

**Every `INSERT INTO entity_identities` in `origin/main`** (non-test) — all seven are machine provenance, none user-asserted:

| Site | Provenance |
|---|---|
| `auth/subject-identities.ts:60` | `auth:signup` — `auth_user_id` + `email` |
| `auth/subject-identities.ts:107` | `auth:signup` — Slack adoption |
| `tools/save_content.ts:326` | `save_content` — self-heals `auth_user_id` from an email match |
| `utils/canvas-events.ts:161` | lazy canvas entity |
| `utils/entity-link-upsert.ts:512` | `connector:<key>` — connector sync |
| `utils/member-entity.ts:136` | member provisioning |
| `utils/promote-keyed-entities.ts:424` | keyed promotion |

One adjacent thing worth knowing: better-auth's own `accountLinking` is enabled (`auth/index.tsx:293-303`, `trustedProviders` = configured socials + generic-OAuth ids, `updateUserInfoOnLink: true`). The login page surfaces this as the `account_not_linked` path — "This social account matches an existing Lobu user. ## 3. Identity engine reach — live, not shadow, but nearly inert downstream

**It is wired into a live code path.** `scheduleIdentityIngest` fires from better-auth's `account.create.after` (`auth/index.tsx:893`) and `account.update.after` (`:933`); `scheduleIdentityTombstoneOnAccountDelete` from `account.delete.after` (`:943`). All fire-and-forget — sign-in never blocks (`identity/auth-hook.ts:180-242`). Routing is registry-based; `auth-hook.ts:19` side-effect-imports `./connectors/google`, the only registered connector.

**It is NOT in shadow mode.** `IDENTITY_ENGINE_SHADOW` appears in exactly two places in all of `origin/main` — `identity/engine.ts:16, 113` and `identity/types.ts:31`. It is absent from `.env.example`, `charts/`, and `.github/`. The predicate is `process.env.IDENTITY_ENGINE_SHADOW === "true"` (`engine.ts:111-114`), so unset ⇒ **shadow off ⇒ full mode, derivations and revocations run.** Caveat: the helm chart mounts an out-of-repo Secret via `envFrom`, so an operator *could* have set it in the cluster. **Unverified from the repo** — worth a `kubectl get secret` check.

What shadow would actually suppress is narrow: facts, supersedes, and tombstones are written either way; only step 4 (revoke derivations) and step 5 (apply `auto_create_when` rules) are skipped (`engine.ts:742-751`). So "turning it on" is not a meaningful lever — the engine is already at full power.

**But its blast radius is nearly nil.** `identity_fact` events have exactly two readers in `origin/main`: the engine's own prior-fact query (`engine.ts:278`) and the tombstone-on-delete lookup (`auth-hook.ts:265`). No authz gate, no routing, no read path consumes them. The only externally visible effect is derived relationships from `auto_create_when` rules — and those require an org to have authored rules via `manage_entity_schema` (`packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-entity-schema.ts:6-24`), plus a `targetField` declared `x-identity-namespace` (`findEntitiesByMetadataField` bails with a warn otherwise). **Whether any prod org has such rules is DB state I could not check.**

So concretely, "turning it on" would mean: registering emitters for github/microsoft/slack/twitter in `identity/connectors/`, and authoring `auto_create_when` rules. Neither is an env flag.

## 4. Claim collision — the premise doesn't match the code

`CLAIM_COLLISION_SEMANTIC_TYPE` (`packages/connector-sdk/src/identity-types.ts:281`) does **not** mean "two entities claim the same identity."

Read `engine.ts:830-847` with `findEntitiesByMetadataField` (`engine.ts`, scoped `WHERE e.organization_id = catalogOrgId AND e.metadata->>${field} = ${normalizedValue}`, no entity-type filter) and `validateTypeRule(relationshipTypeId, memberEntityId, match.entityId)`: `memberEntityId` is the FROM side, `match.entityId` the TO side. A collision fires when **one member's verified fact matches ≥2 candidate TARGET entities** under `matchStrategy: "unique_only"` — e.g. an `email_domain` of `acme.com` matching two `company` rows. It is ambiguous relationship-target resolution, not identity contention.

**This is a bug worth flagging.** The event body at `engine.ts:513` says:

```
content: `Two or more candidate $member rows match this provider-verified ${fact.namespace}; manual resolution required.`
```

and the title is `Identity match collision on ${fact.namespace}`. The candidates are not `$member` rows. Any human who reads this card will diagnose the wrong problem.

**There is no human review surface for collisions.** `recordCollision` (`engine.ts:461-519`) writes an `events` row with `interaction_type: 'approval'`, `interaction_status: 'pending'`, `entity_ids: candidateEntityIds`, idempotent on `origin_id = claim_collision:<connectorKey>:<providerStableId>:<namespace>:<normalizedValue>` (deliberately keyed off the provider id, not the re-issuable better-auth account row id). Then nothing reads it. `git grep -n "CLAIM_COLLISION\|claim_collision" origin/main` returns only: the SDK constant, its two re-exports, `engine.ts`, `types.ts`, and the integration test. Zero hits in `packages/owletto`.

The entity-merge review surface does **not** cover it. Approve/reject in owletto is `run_id`-based (`packages/owletto/src/lib/api/agents.ts:804-906`), and `manage_operations` only resolves `semantic_type = 'operation'` (`:1584`) and `'change_set'` (`:3083`). A `claim_collision` row has neither a run nor a handled semantic type. It would render as a generic pending-approval card in an entity's events tab (`packages/owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/events-tab/event-card.tsx:1702`) with no working action — a permanent pending row.

**What actually happens on genuine identity contention** (two entities, one identifier) is entirely separate and silent:

- `entity_identities` has a live-unique index on `(organization_id, namespace, identifier) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`. Every writer uses `ON CONFLICT … DO NOTHING` — first writer wins, silently.
- Slack is the one place that inspects the loss: `adoptSlackIdentityOntoMember` takes over only from a `person` entity; a claim already held by a different `$member` returns `"conflict"` and produces a `log.warn` (`subject-identities.ts:386-403`) — "two humans cannot share one workspace account, so this is a data problem a person must look at." A log line is the entire review surface.
- The nearest thing to monitoring is `packages/server/src/scheduled/member-claim-drift.ts`, which counts `missing_claim` / `poison_claim` and is explicitly read-only ("the smoke detector, NOT the repair").

## 2. Jira / Linear

**Both are present.** `packages/connectors/src/jira.ts` (790 lines) and `linear.ts` (511 lines) — full OAuth data connectors with virtual (live JQL/GraphQL pushdown) and collected (`sync()`) feeds.

**Neither participates in identity in any way.** No `attributions`, no `*-identity.ts` module, not in `ACL_SOURCES` (`authz/sources.ts:15`), not in `CONNECTOR_IDENTITY_MODULES` (`connector-identity-modules.ts:27`), not in the capability registry.

### As identity producers — unusually cheap, because they already fetch the joinable key
Both already retrieve email and then **discard it into a display string**:
- Jira: `JiraUser.emailAddress` (`jira.ts:74`) → `actorName` returns `displayName ?? emailAddress` (`jira.ts:157`) → stamped as `author_name` (`jira.ts:661`) and `assignee`/`reporter` (`jira.ts:638-639`).
- Linear: GraphQL explicitly selects `assignee { name displayName email }` (`linear.ts:93`) → `actorName` returns `displayName ?? name ?? email` (`linear.ts:99`) → `author_name` (`linear.ts:470`), `assignee` (`linear.ts:453`).

Because the target namespace is the **generic** `email` (`identity-namespaces.ts:52-58`, already `eventRecallIndexed: true` with an existing index), this needs **no new namespace, no new connector-identity module, and no migration**. The change is:
1. Stamp `metadata.reporter_email` / `metadata.assignee_email` alongside the existing display fields (`jira.ts:635-670`, `linear.ts:450-480`).
2. Add an `EventAttributionRule` on the feed's `eventKinds`, copying the Gmail shape verbatim (`google_gmail.ts:183-212`) — `role: 'authored_by'`, `identities: [{ namespace: 'email', eventPath: 'metadata.reporter_email' }]`.
3. Decide `autoCreate`. Gmail gates on `createWhen: metadata.replied === true` to avoid minting a person per no-reply sender (`google_gmail.ts:196`). For Jira/Linear every actor is a real workspace colleague, so `autoCreate: true` unconditionally is defensible — but that's a product call, not a mechanical one.

**Provider-knowledge caveat (unverified against live APIs):** Jira Cloud **redacts `emailAddress` by default** under its GDPR privacy model — it returns `null` unless the app holds `read:jira-user` *and* the user's profile visibility permits it. The field being typed at `jira.ts:74` is not evidence it's populated in production. Linear's `User.email` is generally returned for workspace members under the standard `read` scope. **Before building this, dump one live payload from each and check whether email is actually non-null.** If Jira's is systematically null, the fallback identity is `accountId` (`jira.ts:75`, currently unused) as a new `jira_account_id` namespace — which then *does* require a connector-identity module and, if recall-indexed, a migration.

### As ACL sources
- **Linear maps cleanly.** `teams { id key members { id email } }` gives resource × complete audience, exactly the `AccessResource` shape (`acl-source.ts:57-63`). A `linearAclSource: AclSourceDef` with `resourceNamespace: 'linear_team_key'` and `memberIdentities: [{namespace:'email', primary:true}]` plus a `linearTeamsToResources()` would be a near-mechanical copy of `githubReposToResources` (`github-identity.ts:140-158`), and an `authz/linear-acl-sync.ts` copying `github-acl-sync.ts:94-97`.
- **Jira does not map cleanly.** Its permission scheme (project roles → actors, which may be groups, plus issue-level security levels) is a materially richer model than "collaborators", and flattening it to a member list will silently over-grant. I'd treat Jira ACL as a separate design task, not a copy of the GitHub source.

Neither should be an ACL source *until* it's an identity producer — an ACL source whose members carry no identity the rest of the graph recognizes gates nothing.

## 3. The generic gap — is the switch the right seam?

**No, and the repo already contains the general mechanism — `buildSenderIdentity`'s Slack case is a verbatim duplicate of it.**

Compare:

```
sender-identity.ts:44-56          slack-identity.ts:110-120
  normalizeSlackUserId(teamId,      buildUserKey: (teamId, userId) =>
    authorId)                         normalizeSlackUserId(teamId, userId)
  namespace: SLACK_IDENTITY          userNamespace: SLACK_IDENTITY.USER_ID
    .USER_ID
```

`ChannelReadIdentity` (`connector-sdk/src/acl-source.ts:87-118`) already carries **exactly** the three things `buildSenderIdentity` needs — `platform`, `userNamespace`, `buildUserKey(teamId, userId)` — it is connector-owned (`slack-identity.ts:110-126`), collected in a platform-keyed registry (`authz/sources.ts:31-42`), and has a working lookup helper `channelReadIdentityFor(platform)`. The entire switch reduces to:

```ts
const model = channelReadIdentityFor(sender.platform);
if (!model) return null;
const key = model.buildUserKey(sender.teamId, sender.authorId);
if (!key) return null;
return { identities: [{ namespace: model.userNamespace, identifier: key,
                        matchOnly: false, primary: false }],
         mintEntityType: 'person' };
```

`mintEntityType: 'person'` is a constant across all platforms today, so nothing is lost.

**The one real objection:** `CHANNEL_READ_IDENTITIES` is documented as *"Chat platforms whose per-channel read gate is **enforced**"* (`authz/sources.ts:28-31`), and it is consumed by `channel-visibility.ts:169` and `channel-messages-visibility.ts:60` to build the visibility gate. Adding Telegram there to get sender attribution would **also switch on a channel read gate for Telegram** — and since Telegram membership can't be enumerated from the Bot API (Q1), that gate would have an empty `member_of` graph and deny everything. Attribution and read-gating are genuinely different capabilities and must not be coupled through one list.

**Recommended shape:** keep `ChannelReadIdentity` as-is for the read gate, and add a separate, smaller optional hook for attribution. The natural home is `ChatPlatformDescriptor` (`gateway/connections/platforms/types.ts:53-57`), whose contract already states *"Adding a platform means adding one module under `./platforms/` and registering it in `./index.ts` — no manager edits"* — every other per-platform capability (`extractRoutingInfo`, `createFileHandler`, `getInstructionProvider`, `configureWebhook`) is already an optional hook there, and `sender-identity.ts`'s switch is the last platform-dispatching `switch` left on this path. Add `buildSenderIdentity?(sender): SenderIdentitySpec | null`, have `platforms/slack.ts` delegate to `slackChannelReadIdentity`, and `sender-identity.ts` becomes `getPlatformDescriptor(platform)?.buildSenderIdentity?.(sender) ?? null`.

**What a second platform must duplicate today** (the cost of leaving the switch): a `*-identity.ts` module (namespaces + normalizer + `ConnectorIdentityModule`), an entry in `CONNECTOR_IDENTITY_MODULES`, a `case` in the switch, a rewrite of the pinned negative test, and — if it declares any recall namespace — a migration or CI/startup fails. Steps 1, 2, and 5 are irreducible (they're the connector genuinely declaring new vocabulary). Steps 3 and 4 are pure duplication that the hook removes.

# Identity linking, sign-in providers, and the identity engine — findings

All absence claims below verified with `git fetch -q origin && git grep <pattern> origin/main` (repo at `1f5213b3d`). Owletto is a submodule, so `git grep origin/main -- packages/owletto/**` returns nothing by design; I grepped inside the submodule checkout separately (`packages/owletto` @ `49a9909d`).

## 1. Is there a user-facing account-linking surface? — YES, one, and it is not the one you'd expect

The premise "no linking surface" is **wrong**, but the surface that exists writes to a *completely different table* than `entity_identities` and never touches the `$member` entity graph.

**The `/lobu link <code>` flow** — a signed-in human proving "this chat account is me":

- Mint: `POST /api/:orgSlug/preview/claims` (`packages/server/src/index.ts:1076` → `createPreviewClaim`, `packages/server/src/preview/slack.ts:131`), called by the CLI's `lobu run` (`packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts:803`) under `mcpAuth`. The code lives in `oauth_states`, scope `slack-preview-claim`, 15-min default TTL (`preview/slack.ts:32-36`).
- Redeem: the user pastes the code from their chat account. Two entry points — slash command dispatch, and plain message text for DMs where Slack won't deliver a slash command (`packages/server/src/gateway/connections/message-handler-bridge.ts:1013-1031`, gated on `connection.settings.previewMode === true`).
- Write: `packages/server/src/preview/slack.ts:386-395` calls `linkChatUserIdentity({ platform, teamId, platformUserId, lobuUserId: claim.createdBy })`.

**Target table is `chat_user_identities`**, not `entity_identities`: `packages/server/src/lobu/stores/chat-identity.ts:60-77`. PK `(platform, team_id, platform_user_id)`, FK to `"user"(id)` (`db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:655, 2748, 4691`). The module docblock explicitly states it is platform-agnostic ("Slack, Telegram, or a custom connector all link the same way") and explicitly **not** cross-platform consolidation.

Despite platform-agnostic plumbing, the only platforms reachable today are Slack and Telegram — `PREVIEW_PLATFORMS = MANAGED_CHAT_PLATFORMS_SET` with join defaults for exactly those two (`preview/slack.ts:38-46`). No Discord/GitHub path.

The provenance is honest about being weak. `preview/slack.ts:374-385`:
> "The code was minted by an authenticated `lobu run` and is ASSUMED to be redeemed by the same person… a claim code is effectively a credential for the minter's account — never paste one in a shared channel… **Real identity proof (Slack OAuth / email match) is a follow-up.**"

The takeover guard is the `ON CONFLICT … WHERE chat_user_identities.lobu_user_id = EXCLUDED.lobu_user_id` predicate (`chat-identity.ts:70-76`) — an already-linked triple is never silently re-bound.

Second writer of the same table: `packages/server/src/gateway/connections/slack-claim.ts:197, 230` (Slack workspace-install claim), hardcoded `platform: "slack"`.

**What does NOT exist** (each verified against `origin/main`):

- No settings UI. `packages/owletto/src/app/account/settings.tsx` is Profile (read-only name/email/user id) + Sign Out — nothing else. No `identit*` hits anywhere in owletto that relate to account linking.
- No REST route. `git grep -rln "identit" origin/main -- 'packages/server/src/gateway/routes/**'` → 7 files, all agent-config / agent / agents / app-install / app-webhooks / github-team-graph / github-webhook-actor; none is a linking endpoint.
- No MCP tool. `manage_entity` has merge/unmerge (which *move* identities) but no add-identity operation (`packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-entity.ts`). Tool list at `packages/server/src/tools/admin/index.ts:125-263`.
- `git grep -rniE "link_identity|linkIdentity|claimIdentity|claim_identity|verifyIdentity|verify_identity|addIdentity|add_identity|manage_identities|identity_link|account_link" origin/main` → one hit, an unrelated better-auth error code string at `packages/server/src/auth/index.tsx:851`.

**Every `INSERT INTO entity_identities` in `origin/main`** (non-test) — all seven are machine provenance, none user-asserted:

| Site | Provenance |
|---|---|
| `auth/subject-identities.ts:60` | `auth:signup` — `auth_user_id` + `email` |
| `auth/subject-identities.ts:107` | `auth:signup` — Slack adoption |
| `tools/save_content.ts:326` | `save_content` — self-heals `auth_user_id` from an email match |
| `utils/canvas-events.ts:161` | lazy canvas entity |
| `utils/entity-link-upsert.ts:512` | `connector:<key>` — connector sync |
| `utils/member-entity.ts:136` | member provisioning |
| `utils/promote-keyed-entities.ts:424` | keyed promotion |

One adjacent thing worth knowing: better-auth's own `accountLinking` is enabled (`auth/index.tsx:293-303`, `trustedProviders` = configured socials + generic-OAuth ids, `updateUserInfoOnLink: true`). The login page surfaces this as the `account_not_linked` path — "This social account matches an existing Lobu user. Sign in with a magic link to verify ownership, then continue" (`packages/owletto/src/app/auth/login.tsx:76, 111, 167-172`). That links an OAuth provider to a *better-auth user*, and because it fires `account.create.after`, it does indirectly trigger the Slack adoption + identity ingest.
